definition_zh: 短吻鳄；美洲鳄；扬子鳄；鳄皮革；鳄皮状龟裂
definition_en: a large reptile with a broad rounded snout, found in the southern United States and in part of China; also its leather or a similar scaly crackle pattern
core_image: 趴在沼泽里只露出眼睛和鼻孔的那条长影
scene: 船靠近岸边时，水面浮起一段木头，忽然眨了一下眼。 An alligator lay half sunk in the reeds.
sceneCN: 这里 alligator 是「短吻鳄」（第 1 个义项：吻部宽短的大型爬行动物，产于美洲与中国）；句意为一条短吻鳄半沉在芦苇丛里。核心画面是趴在沼泽里只露出眼睛和鼻孔的那条长影。

derivatives.zh: 加 -ed 构成，义为「像鳄皮一样龟裂的」
加 -ing 构成，义为「漆面鳄皮状开裂」
口语截短形式，义为「短吻鳄」

senses.title: A broad-snouted crocodilian
senses.definition: a large reptile with a wide, rounded snout, found in the southern United States and in a small part of China
senses.definitionCN: 吻部宽而圆的大型爬行动物，分布于美国南部与中国的一小片地区
senses.example: The alligator basked on the bank without moving.
senses.exampleCN: 那条短吻鳄趴在岸边一动不动。
senses.why: The name came from Spanish el lagarto, the lizard, so English alligator is literally the lizard with the article glued on.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字来自西班牙语 el lagarto「那只蜥蜴」，所以英语 alligator 字面就是「把冠词粘在一起的蜥蜴」。

senses.title: Leather with a scaled pattern
senses.definition: the skin of the animal used as leather, or any surface cracked into a similar scaly pattern
senses.definitionCN: 用作皮革的这种动物的皮，或任何裂成类似鳞状纹路的表面
senses.example: The old varnish had turned to alligator across the panel.
senses.exampleCN: 旧清漆在整块面板上裂成了鳄皮纹。
senses.why: Here the animal name transfers to the pattern its skin makes, the same way crocodile is used for a crackle finish.
senses.whyCN: 这里动物名转移到它皮肤形成的纹路上，正如 crocodile 也被用来指龟裂漆面。

intro.en: Alligator is a Spanish phrase swallowed whole: el lagarto, the lizard, was applied to the big reptile of the Americas, and English wore it down into one word.
intro.cn: alligator 是一个被整个吞下的西班牙语短语：el lagarto「那只蜥蜴」被用来称呼美洲的大爬行动物，英语把它磨损成一个词。

items.en: Latin lacertus meant lizard, a word still used in zoology for the genus Lacerta.
items.cn: 拉丁语 lacertus 意为蜥蜴，动物学中仍用于 Lacerta 属。

items.en: Spanish lagarto developed from lacertus and named any lizard, large or small.
items.cn: 西班牙语 lagarto 由 lacertus 演变而来，指任何蜥蜴，无论大小。

items.en: Spanish speakers in the Americas called the big reptile el lagarto, the lizard, with the definite article attached.
items.cn: 美洲的西班牙语使用者把这种大爬行动物叫作 el lagarto「那只蜥蜴」，带着定冠词。

items.en: English sailors and settlers heard the phrase as one word and wrote alligator by the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 英语水手与移民把这个短语听成一个词，到十七世纪已写作 alligator。

items.en: The word now names two living species and, by extension, the scaly leather and the crackle pattern that resembles it.
items.cn: 该词如今指两个现存物种，并引申指鳞状皮革与类似的龟裂纹路。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps words of similar spelling; the near-meaning group lists other crocodilians and the wider class.
note.cn: 形近组保留拼写相近的词；近义组列出其他鳄类与更大的类别。

entries.definition: A claim that someone did wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 指称某人做了错事的说法。

entries.definition: To repeat the same opening sound.
entries.definitionCN: 重复相同的起首音。

entries.definition: One that assigns resources.
entries.definitionCN: 分配资源的人或程序。

entries.definition: One that collects items into a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 把条目聚成整体的人或程序。

entries.definition: A long-snouted crocodilian.
entries.definitionCN: 长吻的鳄类动物。

entries.definition: A smaller Central American crocodilian.
entries.definitionCN: 中美洲一种较小的鳄类。

entries.definition: A fish-eating crocodilian with a thin snout.
entries.definitionCN: 吻细长的食鱼鳄类。

entries.definition: A cold-blooded animal with scales.
entries.definitionCN: 有鳞片的冷血动物。

normalIntro.en: Alligator is Spanish el lagarto, the lizard, run together into one English word.
normalIntro.cn: alligator 就是西班牙语 el lagarto「那只蜥蜴」连读成一个英语词。

normal.en: The al- at the start is the Spanish article el, not the Arabic al- of algebra.
normal.cn: 开头的 al- 是西班牙语冠词 el，不是 algebra 里那个阿拉伯语 al-。

normal.en: Alligators have a broad U-shaped snout; crocodiles have a narrower V-shaped one.
normal.cn: 短吻鳄的吻宽而呈 U 形，鳄鱼的吻较窄呈 V 形。

normal.en: Only two species survive: the American and the Chinese alligator.
normal.cn: 现存的只有两种：美洲短吻鳄与扬子鳄。

normal.en: It is countable, so say three alligators in the marsh.
normal.cn: 它可数，所以说 three alligators in the marsh。

normal.en: Alligatored paint describes a crackle pattern, not a real animal.
normal.cn: alligatored paint 说的是龟裂纹路，不是真的动物。

abstract.en: Picture a log that blinks.
abstract.cn: 想象一段会眨眼的木头。

abstract.en: Imagine only eyes and nostrils above the brown water.
abstract.cn: 想象褐色水面上只露出眼睛和鼻孔。

abstract.en: Think of old paint splitting into little scales.
abstract.cn: 想象旧漆裂成一片片小鳞。

examples.en: An alligator slid off the bank into the water.
examples.cn: 一条短吻鳄从岸边滑进水里。

examples.en: The reserve protects the Chinese alligator.
examples.cn: 这个保护区保护扬子鳄。

examples.en: Alligator skin is banned from trade in many countries.
examples.cn: 许多国家禁止鳄皮革贸易。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿里盖特」——阿里（alli）盖（ga）特（tor）：西班牙人说「那只蜥蜴」，连读就成了短吻鳄。

root: 拉丁语 lacertus「蜥蜴」演变为西班牙语 lagarto，美洲西班牙语称这种大爬行动物为 el lagarto「那只蜥蜴」，英语把整个短语连读磨损为 alligator，字面即「那只蜥蜴」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses come from the same skin: one names the animal lying in the marsh, the other names the scaly pattern its hide leaves on leather or on cracked paint.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都来自同一张皮：一个指趴在沼泽里的动物，一个指它的皮在皮革或龟裂漆面上留下的鳞状纹路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long shape half sunk in the marsh
core.cn: 核心意象：半沉在沼泽里的一条长影

branches.en: A broad snout above the water.
branches.cn: 露出水面的宽吻。

branches.en: A nest guarded in the reeds.
branches.cn: 芦苇丛中看守着的巢。

branches.en: A bag made of scaled leather.
branches.cn: 用鳞状皮革做的包。

branches.en: Varnish cracked into little plates.
branches.cn: 清漆裂成一片片小板。

branches.en: Both keep the picture of scales.
branches.cn: 两者都保留鳞片的画面。

intro.cn: alligator 没有真正的英语词缀：它是借来的短语，所以下表列出西班牙语构件与后来加上去的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin lacertus, lizard, became Spanish lagarto; the article el fused to it and English took the whole phrase.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 lacertus「蜥蜴」变成西班牙语 lagarto；冠词 el 与它融合，英语把整个短语取了过来。

definition_zh: n. 天资，天赋；（学习某事的）能力倾向；（考试测出的）潜能
definition_en: A natural ability to learn or do something well, present before training; in testing, the potential a person shows for a particular kind of work or study.
core_image: 还没学就已经对得上的那个槽口
scene: 她没上过课，却一学就会。 She showed a real aptitude for languages.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：aptitude 指训练之前就存在的天资，常与 for 连用指出在哪一方面。

senses.title: Natural readiness to learn
senses.definition: an inborn readiness for a particular skill, so that progress comes faster than training alone would explain
senses.definitionCN: 对某种技能天生的准备度，使进步快得超出训练本身所能解释的程度
senses.example: His aptitude for figures showed up before he could read.
senses.exampleCN: 他还不会认字时就显出了对数字的天赋。
senses.why: The word is apt plus -itude, the state of being fitted, so aptitude names a fit that exists before anyone teaches you.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 apt 加 -itude，即「合得上的状态」，所以 aptitude 指的是在有人教你之前就已存在的那种契合。

senses.title: Measured potential
senses.definition: in education and hiring, the capacity a test estimates for future performance, as opposed to what has already been learnt
senses.definitionCN: 在教育与招聘中，指测试估出的未来表现潜力，与已学到的知识相对
senses.example: The firm replaced the interview with an aptitude test.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司用能力倾向测试取代了面试。
senses.why: Psychology borrowed the word to separate potential from achievement: aptitude looks forward, achievement looks back.
senses.whyCN: 心理学借这个词把潜能与成绩分开：aptitude 朝前看，achievement 朝后看。

intro.en: Aptitude is Latin aptitudo, fitness, from aptus, fitted. Italian attitudine, from the same Latin word, gave English attitude, so the two are relatives.
intro.cn: aptitude 就是拉丁语 aptitudo「合适度」，来自 aptus「合好的」。意大利语 attitudine 出自同一拉丁词，产生了英语 attitude，所以两者是亲戚。

items.en: The chain starts with apere, to fasten, the verb behind apt, adapt and adept.
items.cn: 这条链从 apere「系紧」开始，它是 apt、adapt 与 adept 背后的动词。

items.en: Aptus, the participle, meant fitted or suitable, the state of a part already in place.
items.cn: 分词 aptus 意为「合好的、合适的」，即零件已经就位的状态。

items.en: Adding -tudo, the suffix for a state, gave aptitudo, fitness or suitability.
items.cn: 加上表状态的后缀 -tudo 得到 aptitudo「合适度、适合性」。

items.en: Italian turned the same word into attitudine, which reached English as attitude, a posture of mind.
items.cn: 意大利语把同一个词变成 attitudine，进入英语成 attitude，指心理姿态。

items.en: English took aptitude in the fifteenth century for fitness or natural tendency.
items.cn: 英语在 15 世纪吸收 aptitude，表示「适合性」或「天然倾向」。

items.en: From the 1920s psychologists used aptitude for measured potential, which gave the aptitude test.
items.cn: 自 1920 年代起，心理学家用 aptitude 指测出的潜能，于是有了能力倾向测试。

note.en: The look-alike group centres on attitude, a genuine relative that now means posture of mind, and altitude, which only looks similar; the near-meaning group lists words for talent.
note.cn: 形近组的核心是 attitude：真正的同源词，如今指心理姿态；还有只是形似的 altitude。近义组列出表示才能的词。

entries.definition: A settled way of thinking or feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 固定的看法或感受方式。

entries.definition: Height above sea level.
entries.definitionCN: 海拔高度。

entries.definition: Fitted, suitable, quick to learn.
entries.definitionCN: 合适的；一学就会的。

entries.definition: To change so as to fit.
entries.definitionCN: 改变以使之合适。

entries.definition: Natural skill in an area.
entries.definitionCN: 某方面天生的本领。

entries.definition: Power to do something, learnt or not.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事的能力，不论是否学来。

entries.definition: A handy special skill.
entries.definitionCN: 一项顺手的小本领。

entries.definition: Stylish natural talent.
entries.definitionCN: 有格调的天然才华。

normalIntro.en: Aptitude is apt plus -itude: the state of already fitting, before any teaching begins.
normalIntro.cn: aptitude 就是 apt 加 -itude：在任何教学开始之前就已经合得上的那种状态。

normal.en: Use aptitude for plus the field: for languages.
normal.cn: 用 aptitude for 加领域：for languages。

normal.en: Aptitude is potential; achievement is what you learnt.
normal.cn: aptitude 是潜能，achievement 是已学到的。

normal.en: Attitude means outlook, not talent, despite the shared root.
normal.cn: attitude 指心态而非才能，尽管同源。

normal.en: The fixed pair is aptitude test, never aptitude exam.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是 aptitude test，不说 aptitude exam。

normal.en: It can be countable: several distinct aptitudes.
normal.cn: 它可数：several distinct aptitudes。

abstract.en: Picture a slot already shaped for a part.
abstract.cn: 想象一个已按零件形状开好的槽口。

abstract.en: Imagine a child reading music before lessons.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子还没上课就能读谱。

abstract.en: Think of a test that guesses tomorrow, not yesterday.
abstract.cn: 想象一份预测明天而非清点昨天的测试。

examples.en: The school tests aptitude rather than memory.
examples.cn: 这所学校测的是潜能，而不是记忆。

examples.en: She has little aptitude for figures but great patience.
examples.cn: 她对数字没什么天赋，但极有耐心。

examples.en: His aptitudes were clear long before his grades were.
examples.cn: 他的天资早在成绩显现之前就一目了然。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：apt「合得上」+ -itude「状态」——天生就合得上的状态，就是天资 aptitude。

root: 拉丁语 apere「装上」的分词 aptus「合好的」加状态后缀 -tudo 成 aptitudo「合适度」，经法语入英语作 aptitude；1920 年代心理学用它指测出的潜能。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses name a fit that comes before training: the talent you can see, and the same talent as a test score.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都指训练之前就存在的契合：看得见的天资，以及化作测试分数的同一份天资。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the slot already matches before any lesson begins
core.cn: 核心意象：还没学就已经对得上的那个槽口

branches.en: A child reading music untaught.
branches.cn: 没人教就能读谱的孩子。

branches.en: A feel for numbers before school.
branches.cn: 上学前就对数字有感觉。

branches.en: A test that predicts future skill.

branches.en: Hiring by potential, not by grades.

branches.en: Both look at fit before training.
branches.cn: 两者看的都是训练前的契合。

intro.cn: aptitude 是 apt 加状态后缀 -itude，同一后缀还构成 altitude、magnitude 与 gratitude。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is apere, aptus and aptitudo; Italian attitudine is the same word on a different road.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 apere、aptus 与 aptitudo；意大利语 attitudine 是同一个词走了另一条路。

latinEntries.exampleCN: apere 是整个词族的起点。

definition_zh: 喷发；（火山）爆发；（皮疹）暴发；（牙齿）萌出；（情绪）爆发；突然大量涌现；气体或液体的喷出
definition_en: a sudden bursting out of material, energy or emotion, especially lava and ash from a volcano
core_image: 封闭的岩层被地下压力顶开，灰柱与熔岩同时冲上天空
scene: 观测站的屏幕上，灰柱从火山口骤然升起，值班员抓起对讲机。 The eruption sent a column of ash high above the island.
sceneCN: 这里 eruption 是「喷发」（第 1 个义项：火山把岩浆、火山灰与气体突然喷出）；句意为这次喷发把一根灰柱送到岛屿上空的高处。

pos.zh: 喷发；爆发；突然大量涌现；（情绪）爆发

forms.label: 形容词（喷发的；爆发性的）

derivatives.zh: 喷发的；爆发性的；火成的
喷发（进行中的动作）；正在喷发的

senses.title: A volcanic eruption
senses.definition: a sudden release of lava, ash and gas from a volcano into the air or onto the surface
senses.definitionCN: 火山把岩浆、火山灰与气体突然释放到空中或地表
senses.example: The eruption sent a column of ash high above the island.
senses.exampleCN: 这次喷发把一根灰柱送到岛屿上空的高处。
senses.why: eruption comes from Latin eruptio, a bursting forth, from erumpere, to break out, so a volcano literally breaks out of its crust.
senses.whyCN: eruption 来自拉丁 eruptio「冲出」，出自动词 erumpere「破出」，因此火山字面上就是冲破地壳而出。

senses.title: An outbreak of rash on the skin
senses.definition: the sudden appearance and spread of a rash over the body as part of a disease
senses.definitionCN: 作为疾病的一部分，皮疹在全身突然出现并蔓延
senses.example: Measles brings a widespread eruption that starts behind the ears.
senses.exampleCN: 麻疹会引起一片广泛的皮疹，先从耳后开始。
senses.why: the old medical use is native to the word: Latin eruptio already named skin lesions breaking out, long before it named mountains.
senses.whyCN: 医学用法是这个词固有的：拉丁 eruptio 早在指火山之前，就已经指皮肤病变的暴出。

senses.title: A tooth breaking through the gum
senses.definition: the process by which a developing tooth pushes through the gum and appears in the mouth
senses.definitionCN: 发育中的牙齿顶穿牙龈、出现在口腔中的过程
senses.example: The dentist charted the eruption of the first molars.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医记录了第一磨牙的萌出情况。
senses.why: a tooth physically breaks through tissue, so the same image of breaking out applies without any change of meaning.
senses.whyCN: 牙齿确实顶破组织而出，因此同一个「破出」意象直接适用，词义无需变化。

senses.title: A violent outburst of feeling
senses.definition: a sudden, forceful expression of anger, laughter or other strong feeling
senses.definitionCN: 愤怒、笑声或其他强烈情绪的突然有力表露
senses.example: His eruption of anger silenced the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他怒火的爆发让全场安静下来。
senses.why: what was held under pressure breaks out, exactly as magma does, so the metaphor needs no new vocabulary.
senses.whyCN: 被压住的东西破壳而出，与岩浆完全一样，因此这个比喻不需要新词。

senses.title: A geyser's jet
senses.definition: a periodic burst of hot water and steam from a geyser or hot spring
senses.definitionCN: 间歇泉或温泉周期性喷出的热水与蒸汽
senses.example: The geyser's eruption lasts about four minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 这眼间歇泉的喷发持续约四分钟。
senses.why: pressurised water finds a narrow opening and shoots out, which is the same physical story as a volcano without the magma.
senses.whyCN: 受压的水找到狭窄开口后冲出去，这与火山是同一个物理故事，只是没有岩浆。

senses.title: A sudden flood of something abstract
senses.titleCN: 抽象事物突然大量涌现
senses.definition: a sudden large appearance of praise, data, complaints or similar things
senses.definitionCN: 赞誉、数据、抱怨之类事物突然大量出现
senses.example: The film brought an eruption of praise from critics.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片引来影评人一片赞誉。
senses.why: the count noun was extended to anything that arrives suddenly and in quantity, keeping the image of something bursting out.
senses.whyCN: 这个可数名词被扩展到一切突然且大量到来的事物，保留了「冲出」的意象。

senses.title: A single spot on the skin
senses.definition: one small lesion or pimple on the skin, as counted and described by a clinician
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤上的一处小病变或小脓疱，由医生计数并描述
senses.example: A single eruption appeared on the forearm and faded in a week.
senses.exampleCN: 前臂上出现了一处皮疹，一周内消退。
senses.why: medicine counts what breaks out, so the mass event and the individual spot share one noun.
senses.whyCN: 医学要对冒出的东西计数，因此整体暴发与单个斑点共用同一个名词。

senses.title: Gas or liquid escaping under pressure
senses.definition: a sudden escape of steam, gas or liquid through a weak point or opening
senses.definitionCN: 蒸汽、气体或液体通过薄弱处或开口突然逸出
senses.example: A sudden eruption of steam cracked the pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 蒸汽的骤然喷出使管道开裂。
senses.why: the core event is material breaking out of a container, and a pipe is only a smaller container than a mountain.
senses.whyCN: 核心事件是物质破开容器而出，而管道只是一个比山更小的容器。

intro.en: Eruption comes from Latin eruptio, a bursting forth, from erumpere, built from e-, out, and rumpere, to break. The same rumpere supplies rupture, interrupt, corrupt, abrupt and, through French and Italian, bankrupt.
intro.cn: eruption 来自拉丁 eruptio「冲出」，出自动词 erumpere，由 e-「出」与 rumpere「破」构成。同一个 rumpere 还衍生出 rupture、interrupt、corrupt、abrupt，并经法语与意大利语衍生出 bankrupt。

items.en: Rumpere meant to break or burst; its past participle ruptus supplied the stem rupt- that runs through the whole family.
items.cn: rumpere 意为打破或爆裂；其过去分词 ruptus 提供了贯穿整个词族的词干 rupt-。

items.en: The prefix e-, out, plus rumpere made erumpere, to break out or burst forth, used for anything escaping a container.
items.cn: 前缀 e-「出」加 rumpere 构成 erumpere，意为破出、冲出，用于任何从容器中逸出之物。

items.en: Eruptio named the act of bursting out; medical Latin used it for rashes breaking out on the skin before geology used it for mountains.
items.cn: eruptio 指「冲出」这一动作；医学拉丁语用它指皮肤上暴出的皮疹，比地质学用它指火山更早。

items.en: English borrowed eruption in the seventeenth century, at first chiefly in medical writing about rashes and fevers.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 eruption，最初主要用于论皮疹与热病的医学写作。

items.en: The volcanic sense became dominant later, and the word then spread to geysers, teeth, emotions, crowds of praise and escaping steam.
items.cn: 火山义后来成为主导，这个词随后扩展到间歇泉、牙齿、情绪、如潮的赞誉与逸出的蒸汽。

items.en: Source uncertain (first use only): the earliest English examples are chiefly medical and the date of the volcanic sense is given only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首用义）：最早的英语例证主要是医学用法，火山义的年代只能给约数。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Latin breaking stem; group two holds near neighbours for sudden outbursts and their results.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「破」词干的词；第二组是表示突然爆发及其结果的近义词。

entries.definition: To burst out suddenly; eruption is the noun of that action, so the pair differs only in word class.
entries.definitionCN: 突然冲出；eruption 是这一动作的名词形式，两者只差词类。

entries.definition: Tending to burst out, or produced by an eruption; it describes a quality or origin rather than the event.
entries.definitionCN: 易爆发的，或由喷发造成的；描述性质或来源，而非事件本身。

entries.definition: A tear or burst of a pipe, tendon or membrane; it shares the breaking stem but lacks the outward prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 管道、肌腱或膜的撕裂或破裂；共用「破」词干，但没有表示向外的前缀。

entries.definition: To break into something in progress; the prefix inter- puts the break between two things rather than outward.
entries.definitionCN: 打断正在进行之事；前缀 inter- 让断裂发生在两者之间，而非向外。

entries.definition: A sudden release of strong feeling or activity; it is commoner than eruption for laughter or rage and rare for volcanoes.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈情绪或活动的突然释放；用于笑声或愤怒时比 eruption 更常见，用于火山则少见。

entries.definition: A violent expansion driven by a chemical or nuclear reaction; it implies blast energy, not merely material escaping.
entries.definitionCN: 由化学或核反应驱动的猛烈膨胀；强调爆炸能量，而不只是物质逸出。

entries.definition: A strong sudden wave of air or heat from an explosion; it names the pressure effect rather than the outpouring.
entries.definitionCN: 爆炸产生的突然强气流或热浪；指压力效应，而非喷出物。

entries.definition: The sudden start of disease, war or violence; it overlaps with eruption in medicine but not in geology.
entries.definitionCN: 疾病、战争或暴力的突然开始；在医学上与 eruption 重叠，在地质上则不重叠。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: e- out plus rupt- break: to break out, and the noun names that breaking out.
normal.cn: e-「出」加 rupt-「破」：破壳而出，名词就指这个破出的动作。

normal.en: The rupt- family runs eruption, erupt, eruptive, rupture, interrupt, corrupt, abrupt and bankrupt.
normal.cn: rupt- 词族包括 eruption、erupt、eruptive、rupture、interrupt、corrupt、abrupt、bankrupt。

normal.en: Volcano phrases: a volcanic eruption, an explosive eruption, the eruption column.
normal.cn: 火山搭配：火山喷发、爆炸式喷发、喷发柱。

normal.en: Medical use survives: a skin eruption, a drug eruption, the eruption of a tooth.
normal.cn: 医学用法仍在：皮疹、药疹、牙齿萌出。

normal.en: Word class pair: lava erupts, so the result is an eruption; the verb is erupt, not erupt.
normal.cn: 词类配对：岩浆喷出，结果就是一次喷发；动词是 erupt，名词才是 eruption。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed jar of fermenting liquid with a crack in the lid.
abstract.cn: 想象一只密封的发酵罐，盖子上有一道裂缝。

abstract.en: Picture a classroom where one joke sets off a wave of laughter.
abstract.cn: 想象一间教室，一个笑话引发一阵笑声。

abstract.en: Picture an inbox that goes from two messages to hundreds overnight.
abstract.cn: 想象一个收件箱，一夜之间从两封变成数百封。

examples.en: The eruption forced the airline to cancel every flight to the island.
examples.cn: 这次喷发迫使航空公司取消了所有飞往该岛的航班。

examples.en: A drug eruption covered her arms within hours of the first dose.
examples.cn: 首剂用药后数小时内，药疹就布满了她的双臂。

examples.en: The announcement produced an eruption of questions from the audience.
examples.cn: 这项宣布引来听众一片问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「e（出）＋rupt（破）」——压力从里面破壳而出 → 喷发、爆发

root: 拉丁 eruptio ← erumpere（e-「出」+ rumpere「破」）→ eruption；同族含 erupt、rupture、interrupt、corrupt、abrupt、bankrupt。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep one gesture: something held inside breaks out. The event is volcanic, then medical, dental, emotional, geothermal, statistical, a single lesion, and finally any pressurised fluid.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项保留同一个动作：被关在里面的东西破壳而出。这个事件先是火山的，然后是医学的、牙齿的、情绪的、地热的、数量上的，再到单个病灶，最后是任何受压流体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sealed layer splitting and material shooting upward and outward.
core.cn: 核心意象：封闭的岩层裂开，物质向上向外冲出。

branches.en: PRESSURISED MATERIAL: magma, hot water and steam all escape through an opening.
branches.cn: 受压物质：岩浆、热水与蒸汽都通过开口逸出。

branches.en: SKIN: the mass outbreak and the single spot are two scales of the same medical event.
branches.cn: 皮肤：整体暴发与单个斑点，是同一医学事件的两种尺度。

branches.en: TEETH: a hard object physically breaks through soft tissue.
branches.cn: 牙齿：坚硬之物确实顶破柔软组织。

branches.en: FEELING: what was contained breaks out as anger or laughter.
branches.cn: 情绪：被压住的感受以愤怒或笑声冲出。

branches.en: QUANTITY: praise or data arrives suddenly and in bulk.
branches.cn: 数量：赞誉或数据突然且成批地到来。

intro.en: Eruption is a Latin noun of action: a prefix meaning out, a breaking stem, and a noun suffix, all three visible in the English word.
intro.cn: eruption 是拉丁动作名词：一个表示「出」的前缀、一个表示「破」的词干、一个名词后缀，三者都保留在英语词里。

latinIntro.en: Latin rumpere, erumpere, eruptio and eruptus give eruption, erupt, eruptive, rupture, interrupt, corrupt, abrupt and, through French and Italian, bankrupt.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 rumpere、erumpere、eruptio 与 eruptus 衍生 eruption、erupt、eruptive、rupture、interrupt、corrupt、abrupt，并经法语与意大利语衍生 bankrupt。

items.example: The prefix e- marks movement out of a container.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 e- 标记离开容器的运动。

items.example: The stem rupt- carries the breaking in every word of the family.
items.exampleCN: 词干 rupt- 在词族的每个词里都承载「破」。

items.meaning: the act or result of doing
items.example: Eruptio is the action noun built on the verb.
items.exampleCN: eruptio 是在动词之上构成的动作名词。

items.meaning: a breaking out; a bursting forth

items.exampleCN: 裂缝在毫无预警的情况下喷发。

items.example: The eruptive phase lasted three weeks.
The rupture in the pipe released steam.
items.exampleCN: 管道上的破裂释放出蒸汽。
这份好处使那名职员腐化。

items.example: The meeting came to an abrupt end.

items.structure: banca rotta (Italian, 'broken bench') via French, from Latin rupta
items.example: The firm went bankrupt that winter.
items.exampleCN: 那家公司在那个冬天破产了。

definition_zh: 应用软件；为最终用户完成具体任务而编写的程序；相对于系统软件的一类软件
definition_en: software written to help end users perform particular tasks, as opposed to the system software that runs the machine
core_image: 办公桌上并排摆着表格、邮件与绘图三个窗口，各做各的活
scene: 办公桌上，职员打开表格、邮件与绘图三套程序，各自完成不同的活。 The company replaced its old application software with a browser-based suite.
sceneCN: 这里指供最终用户完成具体任务的程序（第 1 个义项：面向用户任务的软件）；句意为公司把旧的应用软件换成了一套浏览器端套件。图中可辨识物件：表格、邮件窗口、绘图工具、浏览器。

pos.zh: 应用软件；用户任务软件

senses.title: Programs for user tasks
senses.titleCN: 为用户任务编写的程序
senses.definition: software designed to help a person write, calculate, design, communicate or play
senses.definitionCN: 为帮助人写作、计算、设计、沟通或娱乐而设计的软件
senses.example: The company replaced its old application software with a browser-based suite.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把旧的应用软件换成了一套浏览器端套件。
senses.why: Application names the act of applying a tool to a task, and software names the program, so the phrase is a tool for a use.
senses.whyCN: 前一词命名把工具用于任务的动作，后一词命名程序，因此这个短语就是「为某种用途而设的工具」。

senses.title: A mobile app
senses.definition: a program for a phone or tablet, usually downloaded from a store and opened with a tap
senses.definitionCN: 为手机或平板编写、通常从商店下载并点开即用的程序
senses.example: The ticket lives in an application software package on her phone.
senses.exampleCN: 票就在她手机上的一个应用软件包里。
senses.why: The phrase shrinks to a single icon, and the short form app carries the everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语缩成一个图标，短形「应用」承担日常义。

senses.title: A desktop application
senses.definition: a program installed on a personal computer and run in its own window
senses.definitionCN: 安装在个人电脑上、在自有窗口中运行的程序
senses.example: The designers still prefer desktop application software for large drawings.
senses.exampleCN: 设计师处理大幅图纸时仍偏爱桌面应用软件。
senses.why: The personal computer gave the tool a fixed home, and installation became part of the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 个人电脑给了工具一个固定的家，安装于是成为词义的一部分。

senses.title: An enterprise application
senses.definition: a large program or system that runs a company's records, money, staff or supply chain
senses.definitionCN: 运行公司记录、资金、人员或供应链的大型程序或系统
senses.example: The hospital bought enterprise application software for its accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 医院为账务购买了企业应用软件。
senses.why: When many users and rules are involved, the tool grows into an institution and the word grows with it.
senses.whyCN: 当涉及许多用户与规则，工具长成一套制度，这个词也随之长大。

senses.title: A suite of programs
senses.definition: a group of programs sold together and designed to work with one another
senses.definitionCN: 一组一起出售、设计上可相互配合的程序
senses.example: The office suite is application software, not part of the system.
senses.exampleCN: 办公套件属于应用软件，不是系统的一部分。
senses.why: Several tools in one box are still tools, and the phrase covers the bundle.
senses.whyCN: 几件工具装在一个盒子里仍是工具，这个短语覆盖整包。

senses.title: A web application
senses.definition: a program that runs in a browser and is used through a network rather than installed locally
senses.definitionCN: 在浏览器中运行、经网络使用而非本地安装的程序
senses.example: The accounts team moved to web application software last year.
senses.exampleCN: 账务团队去年转向了网页应用软件。
senses.why: The window no longer belongs to the machine; the tool is borrowed from a server.
senses.whyCN: 窗口不再属于本机，工具是从服务器借来的。

senses.title: The category opposed to system software
senses.titleCN: 与系统软件相对的一类
senses.definition: the class of software that serves users, as distinct from the system software that serves the machine
senses.definitionCN: 服务于用户的一类软件，区别于服务机器的系统软件
senses.example: A computer needs both system and application software to be useful.
senses.exampleCN: 一台电脑既需要系统软件也需要应用软件才能有用。
senses.why: The phrase exists mainly to draw a line: one layer runs the machine, the other puts it to use.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语主要用来划线：一层运行机器，另一层让机器派上用场。

senses.title: The work of building such programs
senses.definition: the industry and practice of designing, coding, testing and maintaining programs for users
senses.definitionCN: 为用户程序设计、编码、测试与维护的行业与实践
senses.example: She studied application software development after a degree in mathematics.
senses.exampleCN: 她读完数学学位后去学应用软件开发。
senses.why: Once a class of programs exists, the work of making them becomes a field with its own name.
senses.whyCN: 当一类程序存在，制造它们的工作就成了一个有名字的领域。

intro.en: Application software joins application, from Latin applicare 'to attach', built on ad- 'to' and plicare 'to fold', with software, a twentieth-century English compound of soft and ware. The phrase became common with personal computers; its exact first use is source uncertain.
intro.cn: application software 由 application（拉丁 applicare「贴上」，由 ad-「向」与 plicare「折」构成）与 software（二十世纪英语复合词，soft 加 ware）组合。该短语随个人电脑普及；最早用例来源不确定。

items.en: Latin plicare meant to fold, and it underlies apply, complicate, explicit and replicate.
items.cn: 拉丁 plicare 指折叠，是 apply、complicate、explicit 与 replicate 的基底。

items.en: Applicare meant to attach one thing to another, from ad- 'to' and plicare 'fold', and English apply kept the sense of putting a thing to a use.
items.cn: applicare 指把一物贴到另一物上，由 ad-「向」与 plicare「折」构成，英语 apply 保留「把某物用于某用途」。

items.en: English application named the act of applying and later a formal request, and in computing it named a use of the machine.
items.cn: 英语 application 指应用的行为，后来指正式申请；在计算领域指机器的一种用途。

items.en: The word software was coined in 1958 as a counterpart to hardware, using soft and ware to name programs rather than metal.
items.cn: software 于一九五八年作为 hardware 的对应词被造出，用 soft 与 ware 指程序而非金属。

items.en: From the late 1970s the phrase application software separated programs for users from the system that ran the machine.
items.cn: 二十世纪七十年代末起，这个短语把面向用户的程序与运行机器的系统分开。

items.en: Phones shortened the phrase to app, and browsers made web applications ordinary, so the class now covers installed and borrowed programs alike.
items.cn: 手机把短语缩成 app，浏览器让网页应用普及，这一类如今既包括本地安装也包括远程借用的程序。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds like application software; the second group names neighbouring ideas in the same field.
note.cn: 第一组在形音上与「application software」相近；第二组是同一领域里意思相邻的其他说法。

entries.definition: A use of something, or a formal request; the first element of the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 某物的用途或正式申请，是短语的第一部分。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to put something to use or to make a request.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物用于某处或提出请求的动词。

entries.definition: A person who makes a request, from the same verb but not the computing sense.
entries.definitionCN: 提出申请的人，同出那个动词，但非计算义。

entries.definition: Able to be applied or relevant, from the same folding root.
entries.definitionCN: 可应用或相关的，同出那个「折」词根。

entries.definition: A household machine, originally something attached to a use.
entries.definitionCN: 家用机器，原指附于某种用途之物。

entries.definition: Software that runs the machine, the class opposed to application software.
entries.definitionCN: 运行机器的软件，与应用软件相对的一类。

entries.definition: Any coded set of instructions, whether for users or for the machine.
entries.definitionCN: 任何编码的指令集，无论面向用户还是机器。

entries.definition: The short everyday form for a mobile application.
entries.definitionCN: 移动应用的日常简称。

entries.definition: A group of programs sold and used together.
entries.definitionCN: 一起出售与使用的一组程序。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin folding verb, the real 1958 coinage and real product phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实拉丁「折」动词、真实一九五八年造词与真实产品搭配。

normal.en: Plicare is Latin for fold, so applicare is to fold one thing onto another, and application is putting a tool to a task.
normal.cn: plicare 是拉丁语「折」，因此 applicare 是把一物折贴到另一物上，application 就是把工具用于任务。

normal.en: Software was coined in 1958 as the counterpart of hardware.
normal.cn: software 于一九五八年作为 hardware 的对应词被造出。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the branches: desktop, enterprise, custom and web application software.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出各支：桌面、企业、定制与网页应用软件。

normal.en: The class is defined against system software: one serves the user, the other serves the machine.
normal.cn: 这一类是相对系统软件定义的：一个服务用户，一个服务机器。

normal.en: The short form app now names the mobile member of the class.
normal.cn: 短形 app 如今指这一类的移动成员。

abstract.en: Application software is a tool laid on a task, like a hand on a handle.
abstract.cn: 应用软件是放在任务上的工具，像手握上把手。

abstract.en: The system builds the room; the application decides what happens in it.
abstract.cn: 系统造出房间，应用决定房里发生什么。

abstract.en: Every icon on the desktop is a folded promise of some work being made easier.
abstract.cn: 桌面上的每个图标，都是一句「某件活会变容易」的折起的承诺。

examples.en: She installed application software for editing photographs.
examples.cn: 她安装了用于编辑照片的应用软件。

examples.en: Application software is updated far more often than the system beneath it.
examples.cn: 应用软件的更新远比它下面的系统频繁。

examples.en: The school teaches application software before it teaches programming.
examples.cn: 这所学校先教应用软件，再教编程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「应用 + 软件」——为某件具体的活而设的程序

root: application 来自拉丁 applicare「贴上」，由 ad- 向 + plicare 折；software 是一九五八年为对应 hardware 造出的英语复合词。短语随个人电脑普及，最早用例来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one tool for a task: user programs, a mobile app, a desktop program, an enterprise system, a suite, a web app, the class opposed to system software, and the work of building them.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着同一件「为任务而设的工具」：用户程序、移动应用、桌面程序、企业系统、套件、网页应用、与系统软件相对的一类，以及开发它们的工作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three windows side by side on one desk, each doing a different piece of work.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张桌上并排三个窗口，各干各的一件活。

branches.en: THE TOOL AND THE LINE: software serves a user, and the phrase draws the line against system software.
branches.cn: 工具与界线：软件服务用户，这个短语划出与系统软件的界线。

branches.en: THE HOMES OF THE TOOL: a phone icon, a desktop window and a browser tab are three places the same tool lives.
branches.cn: 工具的住处：手机图标、桌面窗口与浏览器标签，是同一件工具的三个住处。

branches.en: THE ENTERPRISE: many users and rules make the tool into an institution.
branches.cn: 企业：许多用户与规则把工具变成一套制度。

branches.en: THE SUITE: several tools sold together are still tools.
branches.cn: 套件：一起出售的几件工具仍是工具。

branches.en: THE MAKING: designing, coding, testing and maintaining the tools becomes a field of work.
branches.cn: 制造：设计、编码、测试与维护这些工具，成为一项领域。

intro.en: Application software joins the Latin folding verb plicare through applicare with the English compound software.
intro.cn: application software 把经 applicare 而来的拉丁「折」动词 plicare 与英语复合词 software 连在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin plicare gives applicare and English apply, application and appliance; English soft plus ware gives software; the two are joined into a fixed class name.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 plicare 衍生 applicare 与英语 apply、application、appliance；英语 soft 加 ware 构成 software；两者连成固定的类别名称。

items.example: The root of the first element.
English widened it to requests and computing.
items.exampleCN: 英语把它扩展到申请与计算。
英语保留这个直白动词。

items.example: The agent suffix names the person.
The noun names the tool itself.
The second half names made things.

items.example: The clipping carries the everyday sense.

definition_zh: 谈判过程；（尤指）各方为达成协议而依次经历的正式协商阶段
definition_en: the sequence of stages through which parties discuss terms, exchange offers and move toward an agreement
core_image: 会议室长桌两侧各摆一叠文件，中间一只沙漏，纸页被来回推过桌面，边缘已经磨软
scene: 会议室的长桌两侧各摆一叠文件，中间一只沙漏，纸页被来回推过桌面，边缘已经磨软。 The negotiation process stalled for a week over the wording of a single clause.
sceneCN: 这里 negotiation process 指「各方为达成协议而依次经历的一系列协商阶段」（第 1 个义项：从首次接触直至条款谈成的整段讨论）；句意为谈判过程因为一个条款的措辞而停滞了一周。图中可辨识物件：两叠文件、沙漏、长桌、边缘磨软的纸页。

pos.zh: 谈判过程（可数；复数 negotiation processes）

collocations.phrase: the negotiation process between employers and unions
collocations.zh: 雇主与工会之间的谈判过程

derivatives.zh: 谈判；商定（拉丁 negotiari「做生意、交涉」加 -ate，源自 -atus 动词化后缀，语义偏移为「就条件进行交涉」）
谈判（negotiari 加 -tion，源自拉丁 -tio 动作名词后缀，语义偏移为「交涉这一行为」）
谈判者（negotiation 加 -or，源自拉丁施事后缀，语义偏移为「承担交涉的人」）
可协商的（negotiate 加 -able，源自拉丁 -abilis 能力后缀，语义偏移为「可经谈判改动的」）
过程；处理（拉丁 processus 出自 procedere「向前走」，语义偏移为「一段向前推进的流程」）
程序上的（procedure 加 -al，源自拉丁 -alis 形容词后缀，语义偏移为「与步骤规则有关的」）

senses.title: The whole sequence of talks toward a deal
senses.definition: the entire run of discussion from first contact to signed terms, seen as one continuous activity
senses.definitionCN: 从首次接触直至条款签字的整段讨论，被视为一项连续的活动
senses.example: The negotiation process began with a courtesy call and ended with a handshake.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判过程以一次礼节性拜访开始，以一次握手结束。
senses.why: Negotiation names the bargaining and process names the stretch of time, so the pair marks a course rather than a single moment.
senses.whyCN: negotiation 命名讨价还价，process 命名时间跨度，两者组合标记的是一段过程而非一个瞬间。

senses.title: The formal stages of consultation
senses.definition: the ordered steps of an official consultation: agenda, opening positions, working groups, drafting and adoption
senses.definitionCN: 正式协商中按序推进的步骤：议程、开场立场、工作组、起草与通过
senses.example: Delegates complained that the negotiation process had no clear agenda.
senses.exampleCN: 代表们抱怨这场谈判过程没有明确议程。
senses.why: A process can be broken into stages, and official talks are the place where those stages are written down in rules.
senses.whyCN: 过程可以被切成阶段，而正式会谈正是把这些阶段写成规则的地方。

senses.title: The bargaining flow between employers and unions
senses.definition: the routine sequence of claims, counter-offers, conciliation and a settlement or a strike in industrial relations
senses.definitionCN: 劳动关系中提出诉求、回应报价、调解，直至达成协议或发生罢工的常规序列
senses.example: The negotiation process between the union and the management lasted through the summer.
senses.exampleCN: 工会与管理层之间的谈判过程持续了整个夏天。
senses.why: Collective bargaining is scheduled and repeated, so it is the clearest case of bargaining with a recognizable flow.
senses.whyCN: 集体谈判有排期、可重复，因此是「有可辨认流程的讨价还价」最清楚的例子。

senses.title: The track of peace talks
senses.definition: the slow diplomatic sequence by which warring sides move from a ceasefire to a political settlement
senses.definitionCN: 交战各方从停火走向政治解决的缓慢外交序列
senses.example: Observers say the peace negotiation process has stalled over the status of the border valley.
senses.exampleCN: 观察人士说，和平谈判进程因边境山谷的地位问题而停滞。
senses.why: Peace talks are measured in rounds and months, so the word process is almost required to describe them.
senses.whyCN: 和平谈判以轮次和月份来计量，因此几乎必须用 process 来描述它。

senses.title: The rounds of offer and counter-offer
senses.definition: the repeated exchange in which each side tests the other's limit and moves its own position
senses.definitionCN: 各方反复交换条件、试探对方底线并调整自身立场的循环
senses.example: Every round of the negotiation process removed one disputed clause.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判过程的每一轮都去掉了一个有争议的条款。
senses.why: The core of bargaining is iteration, and a process is exactly the shape that iteration takes over time.
senses.whyCN: 讨价还价的核心是反复，而「过程」正是这种反复在时间上呈现的形状。

senses.title: A mediated consultation
senses.titleCN: 由第三方调解促成的协商
senses.definition: a facilitated sequence in which a neutral party shapes the agenda and carries messages between the sides
senses.definitionCN: 由中立第三方安排议程、在各方之间传递信息的协助式序列
senses.example: The mediation turned a shouting match into a workable negotiation process.
senses.exampleCN: 调解把一场互相叫嚷变成了可行的谈判过程。
senses.why: When a third party manages the steps, the process itself becomes visible as a structure rather than a mood.
senses.whyCN: 当第三方来安排步骤时，过程本身就显现为一种结构，而不只是一种情绪。

senses.title: The formation of a contract
senses.definition: the legal sequence of offer, acceptance and drafting through which an agreement becomes enforceable
senses.definitionCN: 经由要约、承诺与起草，使协议成为可强制执行之文书的法律序列
senses.example: Lawyers watched the negotiation process to see when the offer was actually accepted.
senses.exampleCN: 律师们盯着谈判过程，想看清要约究竟何时被实际接受。
senses.why: Law cares about when each step happened, so the same bargaining flow is reread as a chain of legal events.
senses.whyCN: 法律关心每一步发生在何时，因此同一段讨价还价被重读为一串法律事件。

senses.title: Figurative: step-by-step consensus building
senses.titleCN: 比喻：逐步达成共识的过程
senses.definition: any gradual, patient sequence by which a group talks itself into a shared position, as in a family or a committee
senses.definitionCN: 任何群体通过缓慢耐心的谈话形成共同立场的序列，如家庭或委员会中的情形
senses.example: The committee's negotiation process was mostly a long exchange of drafts.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会的那套「谈判过程」其实主要是长时间交换草稿。
senses.why: The metaphor works because any group that must agree repeats the literal shape: proposals, replies, revision, agreement.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻成立，是因为任何必须达成一致的群体都重复着字面结构：提案、回应、修改、同意。

intro.en: The phrase joins two unrelated Latin stocks: negotium is literally 'not leisure', while processus is 'a going forward'. French carried both halves into English before they were paired. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语把两个互不相关的拉丁词源拼在一起：negotium 字面是「不闲」，processus 则是「向前走」。两半都经法语进入英语，之后才被组合。年代均为约数。

items.en: Neg- 'not' plus otium 'leisure' made negotium 'business', literally the absence of leisure.
items.cn: neg-「不」加 otium「闲暇」构成 negotium「事务」，字面即「不闲」。

items.en: The verb negotiari meant 'to carry on business' and, by extension, 'to transact and bargain'.
items.cn: 动词 negotiari 意为「做生意」，并引申为「办理交易、讨价还价」。

items.en: Negotiatio named a business transaction and the handling of it, and it is the direct source of English negotiation.
items.cn: negotiatio 指一笔交易及其办理过程，是英语 negotiation 的直接来源。

items.en: Pro- 'forward' plus cedere 'to go' gave procedere, 'to go forward, to advance'.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 cedere「走」构成 procedere，意为「向前走、推进」。

items.en: Processus named a going forward, an advance or a course of events, and English took it as process.
items.cn: processus 指向前行进、推进或事情的发展进程，英语借入为 process。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin and first date): the deeper origin of otium is source uncertain, and the date when the two words became a fixed English phrase is not recorded.
items.cn: 来源不确定（深层来源与首见年代）：otium 更早的来源属来源不确定；两个词固定组合为英语短语的年份亦无记载。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same bargaining root plus the bare second element, which are routinely confused; group two holds other names for talk that differ in what they stress.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「交涉」词根的形式，外加单独使用的后半部分，常被混用；第二组是侧重不同的其他「谈话」名称。

entries.definition: The bargaining itself or a single session of it; the process is the whole course those sessions make.
entries.definitionCN: 指讨价还价本身或其中一场；而 process 指这些场次连成的整段过程。

entries.definition: The person who does the bargaining, not the course it follows.
entries.definitionCN: 指进行交涉的人，而不是交涉所走的流程。

entries.definition: Open to being changed by talks; it describes a term or a price, not a timetable.
entries.definitionCN: 指可经谈判改动的；它描述的是条款或价格，不是时间表。

entries.definition: Any series of steps; standing alone it says nothing about bargaining or agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 指任何一系列步骤；单独使用时与谈判或协议无关。

entries.definition: The trading of offers, often over price or wages; it names the haggling rather than the schedule.
entries.definitionCN: 指交换条件，常围绕价格或工资；它命名的是讨价还价，而非流程安排。

entries.definition: Assisted negotiation run by a neutral outsider; a process may contain or consist of mediation.
entries.definitionCN: 由中立外部人士主持的协助式谈判；一个过程可以包含或就是调解。

entries.definition: A formal asking of opinions, which may precede bargaining but need not involve offers at all.
entries.definitionCN: 正式征求意见，可在讨价还价之前进行，但未必涉及任何报价。

entries.definition: The press word for a series of meetings; it is looser and often more hopeful than process.
entries.definitionCN: 新闻用语，指一系列会谈；比 process 更松散，也常带有更多期待。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Neg- 'not' plus otium 'leisure' gives negotium 'business': bargaining is what people do when they are not at ease.
normal.cn: neg-「不」加 otium「闲暇」得出 negotium「事务」：交涉正是人们不得清闲时做的事。

normal.en: The first half runs otium, negotium, negotiari, negotiatio, negotiate, negotiation, negotiator, negotiable.
normal.cn: 前半串是 otium、negotium、negotiari、negotiatio、negotiate、negotiation、negotiator、negotiable。

normal.en: The second half runs cedere 'go', procedere 'go forward', processus 'a course', process.
normal.cn: 后半串是 cedere「走」、procedere「向前走」、processus「进程」、process。

normal.en: The two halves are strangers: one is about business, the other about moving forward, and the phrase simply joins them.
normal.cn: 两半原本互不相干：一半讲生意，一半讲向前走，短语只是把它们接在一起。

normal.en: Fixed collocations mark the stages: enter the negotiation process, stall the negotiation process, a lengthy negotiation process.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出阶段：进入谈判进程、使谈判进程停滞、漫长的谈判过程。

abstract.en: Picture a long corridor with doors on both sides, each opening only after the one before it closes.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长走廊，两侧都是门，每一扇都要等前一扇关上才打开。

abstract.en: Picture a rope walked hand over hand across a gap, one grip at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象双手交替握着一根绳横越沟壑，一次只挪一握。

abstract.en: Picture a clock face without hands, only tick marks that someone crosses off one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象一只没有指针的钟面，只有刻度被人一格一格划掉。

examples.en: A credible negotiation process needs a timetable both sides have already accepted.
examples.cn: 一个可信的谈判过程需要双方事先接受的时间表。

examples.en: The document describes the negotiation process in five separate stages.
examples.cn: 这份文件分五个阶段描述谈判过程。

examples.en: Foreign ministers met to restart a negotiation process that had collapsed in the spring.
examples.cn: 各国外长会面，以重启在春季崩溃的谈判进程。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「neg（不）+ oti（闲暇）+ process（往前走）」——不得清闲，一步一步往前走 → 谈判过程

root: 谈判：拉丁 nec/neg-「不」加 otium「闲暇」构成 negotium「事务」，再派生 negotiari「做生意、交涉」与 negotiatio「交易、谈判」；过程：pro-「向前」加 cedere「走」构成 procedere「前进」，其名词 processus 即「进程」。两半不同源。otium 更早来源属来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one course: two sides begin to talk, and the course is then read as formal stages, an industrial bargaining cycle, a peace track, repeated rounds, a mediated sequence, a contract in the making, and finally any group talking itself into agreement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一段进程展开：两方开始谈，这段进程再依次被读作正式阶段、劳资谈判周期、和平轨道、反复的轮次、调解序列、正在形成的合同，最后是任何群体谈出共识的过程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a table, two stacks of paper and an hourglass, where each exchange moves the papers one step closer to a signature.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张桌子、两叠文件与一只沙漏，每一次交换都让纸页向签字靠近一步。

branches.en: WHOLE AND STEPS: a continuous course and its formal stages are the same span seen close up or from above.
branches.cn: 整段与阶段：连续的进程与它的正式阶段，是同一段时间的近看与俯瞰。

branches.en: FACTORY AND BORDER: wages and peace are different subjects for an identical bargaining rhythm.
branches.cn: 工厂与边境：工资与和平是不同题目，走的却是同一种交涉节奏。

branches.en: ROUNDS AND A REFEREE: repetition drives the process forward, and a mediator makes that repetition legible.
branches.cn: 轮次与裁判：反复推动进程前行，而调解人让这种反复变得可见。

branches.en: LEGAL CHAIN: the same flow is reread as offer, acceptance and enforceable text.
branches.cn: 法律链条：同一段流程被重读为要约、承诺与可执行的文本。

branches.en: METAPHORICAL GROUP: any committee repeats the literal shape on a smaller scale.
branches.cn: 比喻群体：任何委员会都在更小的规模上重演这一字面结构。

intro.en: The phrase is built from two unrelated Latin pieces: a negative plus a noun of leisure, and a prefix of forward motion plus a verb of going.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两块互不相干的拉丁材料构成：一个否定成分加一个「闲暇」名词，以及一个表示向前的介词性成分加一个「走」动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin negotium and negotiari supply the first half; procedere and its noun processus supply the second.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 negotium 与 negotiari 提供前半，procedere 及其名词 processus 提供后半。

items.example: The particle turns leisure into its opposite, business.
items.exampleCN: 这个否定成分把「闲暇」变成它的反面，即「事务」。

items.example: The noun supplies the state that business denies.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供「事务」所否定的那种状态。

items.meaning: business; a matter to be done
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词字面上就是「不闲」。

items.example: The verb adds the activity to the noun of business.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把「做事」的活动加在「事务」名词之上。

items.example: The suffix turns bargaining into a named activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把交涉变成一个有名称的行为。

items.example: The noun is the direct ancestor of negotiation.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是 negotiation 的直接祖先。

items.example: The prefix gives the second half its direction.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀给后半部分定下方向。

items.example: The verb supplies the motion inside process.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供 process 内部的「行进」义。

items.example: The noun turns motion into a course of events.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词把位移变成事情的发展进程。

items.example: English keeps the sense of a course run through.
items.exampleCN: 英语保留了「走完一段路」的意思。

items.example: The suffix yields negotiator from the bargaining stock.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由交涉词干造出 negotiator。

latinEntries.meaning: to carry on business, to bargain

definition_zh: n. 日本动画（日本出品或其风格的动画作品）
definition_en: Animation originating in Japan, or drawn in its distinctive style, often with large eyes and stylised features.
core_image: 大眼睛、尖下巴，一格一格动起来的日本画
scene: 他每周追一集，字幕组当天就更新。 Anime has a large following on campus.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：这里指日本出品的动画作品，校园里追看的人很多。anime 在日语里本泛指一切动画。

senses.title: Japanese animation
senses.definition: animation produced in Japan, treated abroad as a distinct medium with its own studios and conventions
senses.definitionCN: 在日本制作的动画，在海外被视为拥有自身工作室与惯例的独立媒介
senses.example: The studio has produced anime for forty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工作室制作日本动画已有四十年。
senses.why: In Japanese anime simply means animation of any kind; English narrowed it to the Japanese product when the works began to be exported.
senses.whyCN: 在日语里 anime 泛指任何动画；英语在这些作品开始出口后，把它收窄为「日本出品的动画」。

senses.title: The style, wherever drawn
senses.definition: a visual style with large eyes and stylised features, used even by studios outside Japan
senses.definitionCN: 大眼与风格化五官的视觉风格，连日本以外的工作室也会采用
senses.example: The series is anime in style but made in France.
senses.exampleCN: 这部剧集是日本动画风格，但在法国制作。
senses.why: Once a look becomes recognisable, its name travels with the look rather than the passport of the studio.
senses.whyCN: 一旦某种外观变得可辨识，它的名称就跟着外观走，而不是跟着工作室的国籍走。

intro.en: Anime is a Japanese clipping of animeshon, borrowed from English animation, which goes back to Latin animare. English then borrowed the clipped form back with a narrower meaning.
intro.cn: anime 是日语对 animeshon 的缩略，而 animeshon 借自英语 animation，后者可追溯至拉丁语 animare。英语又把这个缩略形式借回来，含义更窄。

items.en: Latin animare meant to give breath to, from anima, breath. It is the ultimate source of the whole animation family.
items.cn: 拉丁语 animare 意为「赋予气息」，来自 anima「气息」。它是整个 animation 词族的最终来源。

items.en: English animation named the film technique from the early twentieth century, and the word travelled with the exported films.
items.cn: 英语 animation 从 20 世纪初起指这种电影技术，该词随出口影片一同传播。

items.en: Japanese borrowed animation as animeshon, written in katakana, the script used for foreign loanwords.
items.cn: 日语把 animation 借为 animeshon，用片假名书写，那是用于外来语的字体。

items.en: Japanese shortened animeshon to anime in the 1970s, and in Japan the word covers all animation, domestic or foreign.
items.cn: 日语在 20 世纪 70 年代把 animeshon 缩略为 anime，在日本该词涵盖一切动画，无论国产或外国。

items.en: English took anime back in the 1980s for Japanese work only, a narrower sense than the Japanese original.
items.cn: 英语在 20 世纪 80 年代把 anime 借回，专指日本作品，比日语原义更窄。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the anim- family and the sociological term anomie; the near-meaning group lists neighbouring Japanese and cartoon forms.
note.cn: 形近组保留 anim- 词族与社会学术语 anomie；近义组列出相邻的日本与卡通形式。

entries.definition: The technique of making images move.
entries.definitionCN: 使图像动起来的技术。

entries.definition: To give life or movement to.
entries.definitionCN: 赋予生命或运动。

entries.definition: A breakdown of social norms.
entries.definitionCN: 社会规范的瓦解。

entries.definition: A living creature that moves and feeds.
entries.definitionCN: 会运动并进食的生物。

entries.definition: Japanese comic books and graphic novels.
entries.definitionCN: 日本漫画与图像小说。

entries.definition: An animated film or comic drawing.
entries.definitionCN: 动画影片或漫画。

entries.definition: A cartoon, in casual speech.
entries.definitionCN: 口语中的卡通。

normalIntro.en: Anime is animation clipped in Japanese and borrowed back, so it is the same word with a passport stamp.
normalIntro.cn: anime 是 animation 在日语中被缩略后又借回英语，所以是同一个词多盖了一个出入境章。

normal.en: In Japan anime means all animation; in English it means Japanese animation.
normal.cn: 在日本 anime 指一切动画，在英语中指日本动画。

normal.en: It is usually uncountable: watch anime, not watch an anime, unless you mean one series.
normal.cn: 通常不可数：watch anime；除非指某一部剧集，才说 an anime。

normal.en: Pronounce it with three syllables, not like the English word anime.
normal.cn: 读作三个音节，不要按英语拼读习惯读成两音节。

normal.en: Manga is printed comics; anime is the moving form.
normal.cn: manga 是纸质漫画，anime 是会动的那种。

normal.en: Do not confuse anime with anomie, a sociology term.
normal.cn: 别把 anime 与 anomie「社会失范」混淆。

abstract.en: Picture a word travelling out and coming back shorter.
abstract.cn: 想象一个词出国一趟，回来时变短了。

abstract.en: Imagine large eyes blinking on a hand-drawn face.
abstract.cn: 想象一张手绘脸上大眼睛在眨动。

abstract.en: Think of a style that keeps its name after crossing a border.
abstract.cn: 想象一种风格过了国境仍保留自己的名字。

examples.en: The festival screens classic anime from the 1980s.
examples.cn: 影展放映 20 世纪 80 年代的经典日本动画。

examples.en: She draws in anime style but writes her own scripts.
examples.cn: 她用日本动画风格作画，但剧本自己写。

examples.en: Anime conventions now attract fans from many countries.
examples.cn: 日本动画展会如今吸引多国粉丝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿尼妹」——阿尼（ani）妹（me）：日本动画里那些大眼睛的妹妹角色，就是 anime；比 animation 少了尾巴，是日语缩略。

root: 拉丁语 animare「赋予气息」经英语 animation 借入日语作 animeshon，20 世纪 70 年代缩略为 anime 泛指动画；英语 80 年代借回，专指日本动画及其风格。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one imported look: the Japanese product itself, and the same visual style used anywhere.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一种舶来外观：日本出品的作品本身，以及在任何地方使用的同一视觉风格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: big-eyed Japanese drawings moving frame by frame
core.cn: 核心意象：大眼睛的日本画一格一格动起来

branches.en: A Tokyo studio with forty years of work.
branches.cn: 一间有四十年作品的东京工作室。

branches.en: A weekly series with same-day subtitles.
branches.cn: 一部当天就有字幕的周更剧集。

branches.en: A French series drawn with large eyes.
branches.cn: 一部画着大眼睛的法国剧集。

branches.en: A style copied by studios worldwide.
branches.cn: 一种被各地工作室模仿的风格。

branches.en: One look, first a place then a style.
branches.cn: 同一种外观，先指产地，再指风格。

intro.en: Anime carries the anim- breath root through English animation, and sits beside manga in the same loanword family.
intro.cn: anime 经英语 animation 带着 anim-「气息」词根，并与 manga 同属一个外来词家族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is animare, reached through English animation and Japanese animeshon; the clipping itself happened in Japanese.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 animare，经英语 animation 与日语 animeshon 抵达；缩略这一步发生在日语中。

definition_zh: 对齐；排列成行；（立场、利益的）一致；结盟
definition_en: the arrangement of parts in a correct relative position or in a straight line; also the state of sharing the same goals, interests or loyalties
core_image: 把几样东西推到同一条直线上
scene: 四个轮子不在一条线上，方向盘总是往左偏。 Wheel alignment fixed the pull in ten minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 alignment 是「对齐」（第 1 个义项：把部件调到同一条直线或正确相对位置）；句意为车轮定位十分钟就解决了跑偏。核心画面是把几样东西推到同一条直线上。

derivatives.zh: 去掉 -ment 的动词，义为「使对齐；使一致」
过去分词作形容词，义为「对齐的；立场一致的」
加 non- 构成，义为「不结盟」

senses.title: Arranging things in a straight line
senses.definition: the arrangement of parts in a correct relative position or in a straight line, used of wheels, text, bones and planets
senses.definitionCN: 把各部件调到正确的相对位置或排成一条直线，用于车轮、文本、骨骼与行星
senses.example: Check the alignment of the text before printing.
senses.exampleCN: 打印前检查文本的对齐方式。
senses.why: Align comes from a- plus line, so alignment is simply the state of being on one line: everything shares the same straight edge.
senses.whyCN: align 来自 a- 加 line，所以 alignment 就是「处在同一条线上」的状态：所有东西共享同一条直边。

senses.title: Agreement of aims or loyalties
senses.definition: the state of having the same goals, interests or loyalties as another person or group, used in politics and business
senses.definitionCN: 与他人或团体拥有相同目标、利益或忠诚的状态，用于政治与商业
senses.example: The merger requires alignment between the two boards.
senses.exampleCN: 这次合并需要两个董事会达成一致。
senses.why: The same straight line is now drawn through intentions: when aims point the same way, people are said to be in alignment.
senses.whyCN: 同一条直线如今画在意图上：当目标指向同一方向，人们就被说成处于一致状态。

intro.en: Alignment is align plus -ment: the French ligne, a line, gave align, to put on a line, and English added the result suffix.
intro.cn: alignment 是 align 加 -ment：法语 ligne「线」产生 align「放到一条线上」，英语再加上表示结果的后缀。

items.en: Latin linea meant a linen thread and then a straight line, from linum, flax.
items.cn: 拉丁语 linea 先指亚麻线，后指直线，源自 linum「亚麻」。

items.en: Old French ligne kept the sense of line or row, and gave the verb lignier, to draw lines.
items.cn: 古法语 ligne 保留「线、行列」之义，并派生动词 lignier「画线」。

items.en: French aligner meant to put in a line, built from a-, to, plus ligne.
items.cn: 法语 aligner 意为「排成一行」，由 a-「向」加 ligne 构成。

items.en: English took align in the seventeenth century, first of troops drawn up in a row and of printed text.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 align，先用于列队的部队与排版的文本。

items.en: Adding -ment gave alignment, and the twentieth century extended it from mechanics to the agreement of policies and interests.
items.cn: 加 -ment 得到 alignment，二十世纪把它从机械领域引申到政策与利益的一致。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the line family; the near-meaning group lists other words for agreement or straight arrangement.
note.cn: 形近组保留 line 词族；近义组列出其他表示「一致」或「排成直线」的词。

entries.definition: To put in a line or bring into agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 排成一行或使一致。

entries.definition: Placed in line, or sharing the same aims.
entries.definitionCN: 排成直线的，或目标一致的。

entries.definition: A long thin mark or a row of things.
entries.definitionCN: 细长的标记或一排东西。

entries.definition: Arranged in or following a straight line.
entries.definitionCN: 排成直线的或沿直线的。

entries.definition: The state of sharing the same view.
entries.definitionCN: 持有相同看法的状态。

entries.definition: A pleasing fit between parts or people.
entries.definitionCN: 各部分或人与人之间协调的契合。

entries.definition: Organising parts so they work together.
entries.definitionCN: 组织各部分使其协同运作。

entries.definition: Behaviour matching a standard or group.
entries.definitionCN: 与标准或群体相符的行为。

normalIntro.en: Alignment is align plus -ment: the result of putting things on one line.
normalIntro.cn: alignment 就是 align 加 -ment：把东西放到同一条线上之后的结果。

normal.en: Line is hidden inside align, so alignment always keeps the picture of a straight edge.
normal.cn: align 里面藏着 line，所以 alignment 始终保留「一条直边」的画面。

normal.en: -ment names a result, as in movement and payment, so alignment is what aligning produces.
normal.cn: -ment 表示结果，如 movement、payment，所以 alignment 就是对齐所产生的东西。

normal.en: Physical alignment is of wheels and text; abstract alignment is of aims and policies.
normal.cn: 实物的 alignment 指车轮与文本，抽象的 alignment 指目标与政策。

normal.en: The fixed phrase is in alignment with, not in alignment to.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是 in alignment with，不是 in alignment to。

normal.en: Out of alignment means misaligned, whether of a spine or of two departments.
normal.cn: out of alignment 就是没对齐，无论指脊柱还是两个部门。

abstract.en: Picture four wheels all pointing the same way down a straight road.
abstract.cn: 想象四个轮子在一条直路上全都指向同一方向。

abstract.en: Imagine three arrows released at once and flying side by side.
abstract.cn: 想象三支箭同时射出，并排飞行。

abstract.en: Think of two company plans that overlay without a gap.
abstract.cn: 想象两家公司的计划完全重叠，没有一处缝隙。

examples.en: Poor alignment makes the tyres wear unevenly.
examples.cn: 定位不准会让轮胎磨损不均。

examples.en: The policy is in alignment with the new regulations.
examples.cn: 这项政策与新规定保持一致。

examples.en: The planets reached a rare alignment that night.
examples.cn: 那晚行星出现了一次罕见的排列。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿莱恩门特」——阿莱恩（align）是排成线，门特（ment）是结果：排成一条线的结果，就是对齐、一致。

root: 拉丁语 linea「亚麻线、直线」经古法语 ligne 构成法语 aligner「排成一行」，英语借为 align，再加表示结果的后缀 -ment 构成 alignment，字面即「被放到同一条线上的状态」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one straight line applied twice: to objects it means correct position, and to people it means shared direction, so nothing pulls sideways.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一条直线用了两次：用在物体上指位置正确，用在人身上指方向一致，总之没有任何东西往旁边偏。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several things pushed onto one straight line
core.cn: 核心意象：把几样东西推到同一条直线上

branches.en: Wheels pointing the same way.
branches.cn: 指向同一方向的四个轮子。

branches.en: Text flush against one margin.
branches.cn: 文本齐整地贴着同一边距。

branches.en: Two boards sharing one goal.
branches.cn: 两个董事会共享一个目标。

branches.en: Countries grouping by interest.
branches.cn: 各国按利益结成群。

branches.en: Both remove sideways pull.
branches.cn: 两者都消除了往旁边的偏力。

intro.en: Alignment is built from a- plus line plus -ment, so the spelling itself shows direction, line and result.
intro.cn: alignment 由 a- 加 line 加 -ment 构成，拼写本身就显示出方向、线与结果。

latinIntro.en: Latin linea, from linum, flax, gave French ligne and aligner; English took align and added -ment.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 linea 源自 linum「亚麻」，产生法语 ligne 与 aligner；英语取用 align 并加上 -ment。

items.meaning: the state of being in line

latinEntries.exampleCN: linea 产生 line 与 align。

latinEntries.example: Linum is the plant behind linea.
latinEntries.exampleCN: linum 是 linea 背后的植物。

definition_zh: n. 服装；衣着（尤指正式或特定场合的）；v. 使穿戴；打扮
definition_en: Clothes, especially fine or formal ones worn for a particular occasion; as a verb, to dress someone in such clothes.
core_image: 为某个场合从头到脚配好的一身行头
scene: 请柬上写明要穿正式服装，她于是挑了那件深蓝长裙。 The invitation said formal attire, so she chose the long navy dress.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：attire 指为某个场合准备的整套衣着，语体偏正式。

senses.title: Clothes for an occasion
senses.definition: the clothes a person wears, thought of as a complete set suited to an occasion
senses.definitionCN: 一个人所穿的衣物，被视为适合某场合的一整套
senses.example: Guests were asked to wear evening attire.
senses.exampleCN: 来宾被要求穿晚礼服。
senses.why: Attire came from a verb meaning to put in order, so it names clothes as an arranged whole rather than single items.
senses.whyCN: attire 源自意为「整理妥当」的动词，因此它把衣着看作安排好的整体，而非单件衣物。

senses.title: To dress someone
senses.definition: as a verb, to put clothes on a person, usually in a formal or ceremonial way
senses.definitionCN: 作动词，指给人穿上衣服，通常带正式或礼仪色彩
senses.example: The bride was attired in white brocade.
senses.exampleCN: 新娘身穿白色织锦。
senses.why: The noun and verb grew together, so the passive be attired in is the natural verb pattern.
senses.whyCN: 名词与动词一同发展，因此被动式 be attired in 是最自然的动词句式。

senses.title: Dress that marks a group
senses.definition: a style of dress taken as the mark of a group, period or profession
senses.definitionCN: 被视为某群体、时代或职业标志的一种装束风格
senses.example: The painting records the attire of rural monks.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画记录了乡村僧侣的装束。
senses.why: Because attire already means an arranged whole, it slides easily into meaning the look that identifies a group.
senses.whyCN: 既然 attire 本就指安排好的整体，它便顺势用来指能标识某群体的整体外观。

intro.en: Attire is a- plus tire, an Old French word for rank or order; the verb atirier meant to put in order or equip, and the noun followed from it.
intro.cn: attire 是 a- 加 tire——古法语中表示「行列、次序」的词；动词 atirier 意为「整理妥当、装备」，名词由此产生。

items.en: A Germanic word for adornment or ordered gear stands behind the second half of the word.
items.cn: 一个意为「装饰、成套装备」的日耳曼词是这个词后半部分的来源。

items.en: Old French tire meant a rank or row, the notion of things set out in order.
items.cn: 古法语 tire 意为「行列、次序」，即把东西排列有序的概念。

items.en: Adding a-, to, gave atirier, to put in order, to equip or adorn a person.
items.cn: 加上 a-「向」构成 atirier，意为「整理妥当、装备或打扮某人」。

items.en: Middle English atiren kept both equipping and dressing, and the noun followed from it.
items.cn: 中古英语 atiren 兼有「装备」与「穿衣」两义，名词随之产生。

items.en: By the fourteenth century attire was an ordinary formal word for the clothes a person wore.
items.cn: 到十四世纪 attire 已是指人衣着的常用正式词。

items.en: Today the noun survives mainly in dress codes, while the verb lives on in the passive.
items.cn: 今天名词主要保留在着装规定中，动词则以被动形式延续。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps words that end in the same sound; the near-meaning group lists other words for a set of clothes.
note.cn: 形近组保留结尾读音相同的词；近义组列出表示成套衣着的其他词。

entries.definition: Whole, with nothing left out.
entries.definitionCN: 完整的，无缺的。

entries.definition: To withdraw or stop working.
entries.definitionCN: 退出；退休。

entries.definition: Writing that mocks by wit.
entries.definitionCN: 以机智讥讽的作品。

entries.definition: To bring into harmony.
entries.definitionCN: 使协调一致。

entries.definition: Clothing, especially for sale.
entries.definitionCN: 衣着，尤指商品服装。

entries.definition: Clothing marking a role.
entries.definitionCN: 标识身份的服装。

entries.definition: A set of clothes worn together.
entries.definitionCN: 一同穿的一套衣服。

entries.definition: Clothing, in older writing.
entries.definitionCN: 旧式书面语中的衣着。

normalIntro.en: Attire hides a- plus tire, an old word for order: clothes put in order for the occasion.
normalIntro.cn: attire 里藏着 a- 加 tire——tire 是表示「次序」的旧词：为场合整理妥当的一身衣服。

normal.en: Formal attire is the standard dress-code phrase.
normal.cn: formal attire 是着装规定的标准说法。

normal.en: The noun is uncountable in normal use.
normal.cn: 名词在常规用法中不可数。

normal.en: The verb appears as be attired in.
normal.cn: 动词常见形式是 be attired in。

normal.en: Attire is more formal than clothes.
normal.cn: attire 比 clothes 更正式。

normal.en: Business attire usually means a suit.
normal.cn: business attire 通常指西装。

abstract.en: Picture a whole outfit laid out on a bed.
abstract.cn: 想象一整套衣服摊在床上。

abstract.en: Imagine a robe placed on shoulders in a rite.
abstract.cn: 想象仪式中把长袍披上肩头。

abstract.en: Think of a painting read by its costumes.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅可以凭服饰读懂的画。

examples.en: The staff wore neat business attire.
examples.cn: 员工穿着整洁的商务服装。

examples.en: She was attired in a grey travelling cloak.
examples.cn: 她身穿灰色旅行斗篷。

examples.en: Ceremonial attire is kept in the vestry.
examples.cn: 礼仪服饰存放在圣器室。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：a-「向」+ tire「行列、次序」——把全身衣物按场合排妥当，就是 attire。

root: 古法语 tire「行列、次序」加 a-「向」成 atirier「整理、装备」，入中古英语作 atiren「打扮」；名词 attire 由「整理好的一身」转指服装。

sensesIntro.en: The senses share one idea of a set put in order: clothes chosen for an occasion, the act of putting them on, and the look that marks a group.
sensesIntro.cn: 各义项共享「整理成套」这一想法：为场合挑好的衣服、把它们穿上的动作，以及标识某群体的整体外观。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whole outfit arranged head to foot for one occasion
core.cn: 核心意象：为某个场合从头到脚配好的一身行头

branches.en: A navy dress chosen for a formal card.
branches.cn: 为正式请柬挑的深蓝长裙。

branches.en: Evening clothes requested of guests.
branches.cn: 要求来宾穿的晚礼服。

branches.en: A bride dressed in white brocade.
branches.cn: 身穿白色织锦的新娘。

branches.en: Robes that mark rural monks.
branches.cn: 标识乡村僧侣的袍服。

branches.en: Both treat clothes as one arranged whole.
branches.cn: 两者都把衣着视为安排好的整体。

intro.en: Attire is a- plus tire; the same a- prefix builds arise and awake, while the dress field supplies apparel and garment.
intro.cn: attire 是 a- 加 tire；同一 a- 前缀还构成 arise 与 awake，而服饰义场提供 apparel 与 garment。

latinIntro.en: The word is French rather than Latin: tire, order, and atirier, to equip; Latin ornare, to adorn, gives ornament beside it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属法语而非拉丁语层次：tire「次序」与 atirier「装备」；旁边拉丁语 ornare「装饰」产生 ornament。

latinEntries.example: Tire is the hidden half of attire.
latinEntries.exampleCN: tire 是 attire 隐藏的后半部分。

definition_zh: 立志；渴望达到；谋求职位；向往
definition_en: to desire strongly to achieve something high or to become a certain kind of person
core_image: 一个孩子趴在窗台上，看远处塔楼的尖顶，一直看到脖子发酸
scene: 她十六岁那年看完一本关于深海的书，从此决定要做海洋生物学家。 She aspired to study the deep sea years before any university had replied.
sceneCN: 这里 aspire 指「立志要达到某个高目标」（第 1 个义项：朝高处立志）；句意为在还没有任何大学回信之前，她早已立志研究深海。图中可辨识物件：远处的塔尖、被翻旧的深海书、窗台的手印、尚未拆封的回信。

pos.zh: 立志；渴望（与 to、after 搭配）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加表示行为的名词后缀构成，语义由「朝高处呼气」转为「志向」
由动词词干加表示人的后缀构成，语义由「渴望」转为「谋求者」
由现在分词转为形容词，语义由「正立志」转为「有志于进入某行的」
由名词加形容词后缀构成，语义由「志向」转为「带有志向色彩的、励志的」

senses.title: Aim at a distant goal
senses.definition: to set one's hopes on a goal that lies well beyond present reach
senses.definitionCN: 把希望放在一个远超出当下能力所及的目标上
senses.example: She aspired to study the deep sea long before any university had replied.
senses.exampleCN: 在还没有任何大学回信之前，她早已立志研究深海。
senses.why: the Latin verb means to breathe toward something, so aspiring is aiming one's whole breath at a far object.
senses.whyCN: 那个拉丁动词意为「朝某物呼气」，因此立志就是把整口气都朝一个远处的对象呼去。

senses.title: Seek a particular office
senses.definition: to try to obtain a post, title or place that others may also want
senses.definitionCN: 试图取得一个别人也想要的职位、头衔或位子
senses.example: Three deputies aspired to the vacant chair.
senses.exampleCN: 三位副手都想坐上那把空出的椅子。
senses.why: the Roman picture was a candidate walking around to court votes, and that political sense never left the word.
senses.whyCN: 罗马的图景是候选人四处奔走拉票，那层政治意味从未离开这个词。

senses.title: Want to become a certain person
senses.definition: to wish to turn oneself into a particular kind of person or worker
senses.definitionCN: 希望把自己变成某一类人或某一种从业者
senses.example: He aspired to be a country doctor rather than a famous surgeon.
senses.exampleCN: 他想做乡村医生，而不是名医。
senses.why: the aim is no longer a thing but an identity, and the same upward breath is directed at a self to be built.
senses.whyCN: 目标不再是一件东西，而是一种身份，同一口向上的气被呼向一个待建成的自己。

senses.title: Emulate a standard
senses.definition: to measure oneself against a model or a standard set by others
senses.definitionCN: 拿自己与别人立下的榜样或标准相比照
senses.example: Her early drawings aspired to the plainness of the old masters.
senses.exampleCN: 她早期的素描向往古代大师那种朴素。
senses.why: breathing toward a model is how skill is acquired: one imitates before one can invent.
senses.whyCN: 朝榜样呼气正是技艺获得的途径：先模仿，才谈得上创造。

senses.title: Hope for an ideal condition
senses.definition: to long for a better condition such as peace, fairness or quiet
senses.definitionCN: 渴望更好的处境，如和平、公平或安宁
senses.example: The whole valley aspired to nothing more than a quiet winter.
senses.exampleCN: 整个山谷向往的不过是一个安静的冬天。
senses.why: the object can be a condition rather than a possession, which is why the word suits public hopes.
senses.whyCN: 对象可以是一种处境而非一件所有物，因此这个词适合表达公共的希望。

senses.title: Rise physically
senses.definition: to rise or tower upward, said of buildings, smoke or terrain in older prose
senses.definitionCN: 向上升起或高耸，旧时用于建筑、烟或地形
senses.example: The spire aspired so high that the bells could be heard across the river.
senses.exampleCN: 那尖顶高耸，钟声在河对岸都听得见。
senses.why: this is the plain physical sense of breathing upward, before the word was narrowed to desire.
senses.whyCN: 这是「向上呼气」最朴素的物理义，出现在词义收窄为「渴望」之前。

senses.title: Pronounce with a breath
senses.definition: to utter a consonant with a audible puff of breath, as in the p of pin
senses.definitionCN: 发音时带出一股听得见的气，如某些词里那个辅音之后的气
senses.example: In this dialect speakers aspire the t at the end of a word.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个方言里，说话人会把词尾那个辅音发成送气音。
senses.why: phonetics kept the literal meaning, since the sound really is a breath pushed out.
senses.whyCN: 语音学保留了字面意思，因为那个音确实就是被推出来的一口气。

senses.title: Long for something intensely
senses.definition: to desire something intensely, often used with after in formal prose
senses.definitionCN: 强烈地想要某物，正式文字中后面常接一个介词
senses.example: The exiled poet aspired after one more sight of the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 流亡的诗人心心念念再看一眼那些山。
senses.why: when the object is out of reach, the verb carries pure longing rather than a plan.
senses.whyCN: 当对象无法到手，这个动词就带着纯粹的渴，而不是一份计划。

intro.en: Aspire comes from Latin aspirare 'to breathe upon, to blow toward', built on ad- 'to' and spirare 'to breathe'. The deeper origin of spirare is not settled. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 该词来自拉丁 aspirare「朝……呼气、向……吹」，由 ad-「向」与 spirare「呼吸」构成。spirare 的更深来源尚无定论，年代均为约数。

items.en: Spirare meant 'to breathe, to blow'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the tie proposed to a root for 'to blow' is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: spirare 意为「呼吸、吹」。其更深来源不确定；把它与表示「吹」的词根相联系，只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus spirare gave aspirare 'to breathe upon', and metaphorically to favour someone or to strive toward something.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 spirare 构成 aspirare「朝……呼气」，并比喻为「眷顾某人」或「向往某物」。

items.en: Roman writers used the verb for courting support, so the word entered English with a political edge before it meant plain longing.
items.cn: 罗马作家用这个动词表示争取支持，因此这个词带着政治色彩进入英语，早于它表示单纯渴望。

items.en: English took the verb in the fourteenth century, at first in the sense of rising or towering, then of hoping for high things.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪吸收了这个动词，先表「升起、高耸」，再表「向往高处之物」。

items.en: Grammarians applied the same word to consonants pronounced with breath, which is the oldest physical layer kept in technical use.
items.cn: 语法学家把同一个词用于带气发音的辅音，这是最古老的物理层在技术用语中的保存。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin of spirare and the dating of the hopeful sense): no citation fixes when rising became longing, and any Indo-European form offered for spirare is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（spirare 的更深来源与希望义的确切年代）：没有书证能定住「升起」何时变成「渴望」；凡为 spirare 给出的印欧语形式均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one separates words built on the same breathing verb; group two separates verbs of wanting by how reachable the object is.
note.cn: 第一组区分同出「呼吸」动词的词；第二组按对象的可达程度区分表示「想要」的动词。

entries.definition: In- 'into' plus spirare: to breathe a feeling into someone, hence to fill them with enthusiasm.
entries.definitionCN: 由 in-「入」加 spirare 构成：把某种感受吹进别人心里，因而指激发热情。

entries.definition: Ex- 'out' plus spirare: to breathe out one's last breath, hence to come to an end.
entries.definitionCN: 由 ex-「出」加 spirare 构成：呼出最后一口气，因而指终了、到期。

entries.definition: Com- 'together' plus spirare: to breathe as one, hence to plot together in secret.
entries.definitionCN: 由 com-「共同」加 spirare 构成：同呼一口气，因而指暗中合谋。

entries.definition: Per- 'through' plus spirare: to breathe through the skin, that is, to sweat.
entries.definitionCN: 由 per-「穿过」加 spirare 构成：透过皮肤呼气，也就是出汗。

entries.definition: From Latin asper 'rough': harshness of surface or manner, with no connection to breathing.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 asper「粗糙」：表面或态度的粗硬，与呼吸无关。

entries.definition: To want something with a real chance in view; it can be modest, while aspiring is always aimed high.
entries.definitionCN: 在还看得见机会的情况下想要某事；可以很小，而立志总是朝高处。

entries.definition: To want something, often without any plan to get it; it carries no effort.
entries.definitionCN: 想要某物，往往没有任何获取的计划；不含努力。

entries.definition: To feel a deep and often painful desire; the feeling outweighs the aim.
entries.definitionCN: 怀着深沉而常带痛的渴望；感受压过了目标。

entries.definition: To try actively to find or obtain something; it names the activity rather than the ambition.
entries.definitionCN: 积极地设法找到或取得；指活动，而不是抱负。

entries.definition: To struggle hard toward something; it stresses the exertion, while aspire stresses the height of the aim.
entries.definitionCN: 奋力朝某处挣扎；强调使力，而 aspire 强调目标的高度。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Ad- 'to' plus spirare 'breathe': to breathe toward something far away.
normal.cn: ad-「向」加 spirare「呼吸」：朝远处某物呼出一口气。

normal.en: The family runs aspire, aspiration, aspirant, aspiring, aspirational.
normal.cn: 同族词覆盖动词、名词、谋求者、现在分词形容词与励志形容词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the objects: aspire to a post, aspire to become, aspire after honour.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出对象：谋求职位、渴望成为、渴求荣誉。

normal.en: The political origin survives in aspirant, the person who wants the seat.
normal.cn: 政治来源仍活在「谋求者」这个名词里，指那个想要位子的人。

normal.en: Phonetics keeps the oldest sense: an aspirated consonant is a sound carrying a puff of breath.
normal.cn: 语音学保留了最古老的意思：送气辅音就是带出一口气的音。

abstract.en: Picture a child on a sill looking at a spire until the neck aches.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子趴在窗台上望着塔尖，直到脖子发酸。

abstract.en: Picture a kite pulling at the string before the wind has lifted it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只风筝在风还没把它托起时就已经把线拉紧。

abstract.en: Picture a seed leaning toward a light it cannot yet reach.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子朝它还够不到的光倾斜。

examples.en: Many young engineers aspire to work on the rover team.
examples.cn: 许多年轻工程师立志进入火星车团队。

examples.en: He aspired to the mayor's office for twelve years.
examples.cn: 他谋求市长之位谋了十二年。

examples.en: The village aspired after clean water more than after roads.
examples.cn: 村民对干净用水的渴求胜过对道路的渴求。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「a 斯派尔」——一口气朝远处送去 → 立志、渴望

root: 拉丁 aspirare「朝……呼气」= ad-（向）+ spirare（呼吸）；spirare 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one breath: it is aimed at a goal, at an office, at an identity, at a model, at a condition, at the sky itself, at a consonant, and finally at something simply out of reach.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一口气展开：这口气被呼向一个目标、一个职位、一种身份、一个榜样、一种处境、天空本身、一个辅音，最后呼向一件单纯够不到的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a watcher at a window breathing toward a distant spire.
core.cn: 核心意象：窗前的观望者朝远处塔尖呼出一口气。

branches.en: THE AIM AND THE CONDITION: a distant goal and a wished-for state are the same upward breath.
branches.cn: 目标与处境：远处的目标与所盼的处境，是同一口向上的气。

branches.en: THE CONTESTED SEAT: others want it too, and the political origin shows.
branches.cn: 被争的位子：别人也想要，政治来源在此显现。

branches.en: A SELF TO BUILD: a person and a model are both aims one grows toward.
branches.cn: 待建的自己：人与榜样都是会长过去的靶子。

branches.en: THE LITERAL RISE: stone and smoke go up before desire is meant.
branches.cn: 字面的升起：在「渴望」之前，石头与烟先往上升。

branches.en: BREATH WITHOUT AN OBJECT: a consonant's puff, and longing that has given up on arrival.
branches.cn: 没有对象的气：辅音的那一口气，以及不再指望抵达的渴望。

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb with a prepositional prefix, and both parts still build English words, so it reads clearly by morphemes.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个带介词前缀的拉丁动词，两部分仍在构成英语词，因此可以按语素清楚读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin spirare gives spirit, inspire, expire, respire and conspire; ad- 'to' appears in adapt, adhere and admire.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 spirare 衍生出 spirit、inspire、expire、respire 与 conspire；ad-「向」见于 adapt、adhere 与 admire。

items.example: The prefix gives the breath a direction.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀给这口气一个方向。

items.example: The root is the breathing itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根就是呼吸本身。

items.example: The wind breathed upon the cliff.

items.structure: aspirare passing into French and English
items.example: She aspired to the research post.
items.exampleCN: 她立志争取这个研究职位。

items.example: An aspiring novelist worked the night shift.
items.exampleCN: 一位有志写小说的人上夜班。
