branches.cn: 两者都不肯把对象放着不管。

intro.en: Babysit is baby plus sit; the same compound pattern gives housesit and petsit, and -er turns it back into babysitter.
intro.cn: babysit 是 baby 加 sit；同一复合方式产生 housesit 与 petsit，而 -er 又把它变回 babysitter。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are native rather than Latin; Latin sedere, to sit, gives session and sedentary beside the English sit.
latinIntro.cn: 两个部分都属本族语而非拉丁语；旁边的拉丁语 sedere「坐」产生 session 与 sedentary。

definition_zh: 修改；调整；修饰；缓和；修订；改性
definition_en: to change something in some details or qualities without replacing it entirely, often to make it fit a new purpose or to make it less extreme
core_image: 在一件旧物上按尺寸修整几处，整体仍然是原来那件东西
scene: 工程师没有换掉整只阀门，只改了一个法兰让它接上新管道。 The engineer did not replace the whole valve; she chose to modify one flange so that it would fit the new pipe.
sceneCN: 这里 modify 是「部分修改」（第 1 个义项：改动局部而不整体替换）；句意：工程师没有换掉整个阀门，只改动了一个法兰盘，让它能接上新管道。场景要点：一台拆开的旧阀门、一只被换掉的零件、旁边保留完好的阀体；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 修改；调整；修饰；缓和；修订

senses.title: Change a part, not the whole
senses.definition: to change some details, parts, or qualities of something while leaving its identity and main structure intact
senses.definitionCN: 改动某物的部分细节、部件或性质，同时保留它的身份与主要结构
senses.example: The engineer modified the valve instead of replacing the whole assembly.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师改动了阀门，而不是更换整个组件。
senses.why: Latin modificare joined modus 'measure' to facere 'make': to make according to a measure. The word starts from adjusting a thing's proportions, not from destroying and remaking it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 modificare 把 modus“尺度”与 facere“做”合在一起：按尺度去制作。这个词的起点是调整一件东西的比例，而不是毁掉重造。

senses.title: Adapt to fit a new use
senses.definition: to adjust something so that it suits a different purpose, condition, or user
senses.definitionCN: 调整某物，使其适合不同的目的、条件或使用者
senses.example: The school modified its timetable to fit the bus schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 学校调整了课程表，以配合公交时刻。
senses.why: A measure is taken against a purpose. When the purpose changes, the thing is re-measured and trimmed until it fits again, which is why modify often appears with 'to fit' or 'for'.
senses.whyCN: 尺度总是对着某个目的量。目的变了，东西就被重新量一遍、修一遍，直到重新合身，所以 modify 常与“适应”“为了”一类说法连用。

senses.title: Grammar: a word limits another
senses.titleCN: 语法：一个词限定另一个词
senses.definition: of a word or phrase, to limit or qualify the meaning of another word
senses.definitionCN: 指一个词或短语限定或说明另一个词的意义
senses.example: In 'a red door', the adjective modifies the noun 'door'.
senses.exampleCN: 在 a red door 中，形容词修饰名词 door。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the word for narrowing a meaning. An adjective places a measure on a noun, saying which part of its range is meant, without replacing the noun.
senses.whyCN: 语法学借这个词来表示收窄意义。形容词给名词加上一个尺度，说明指的是它范围里的哪一部分，而不替换这个名词。

senses.title: Soften a claim or tone
senses.definition: to make a statement, demand, or tone less absolute or less severe
senses.definitionCN: 使陈述、要求或语气不那么绝对、不那么严厉
senses.example: He modified his tone when he saw that the child was listening.
senses.exampleCN: 看到孩子在听，他把语气缓和了下来。
senses.why: To keep within measure also means not to exceed it. A demand that is modified has been brought back inside reasonable bounds, so the word can mean 'soften' rather than 'change'.
senses.whyCN: 保持在尺度之内，也意味着不越过尺度。被 modify 的要求被拉回到合理的范围内，所以这个词可以表示“缓和”，而不只是“改变”。

senses.title: Amend a legal text
senses.definition: to make a formal, limited change to a law, contract, or official document
senses.definitionCN: 对法律、合同或正式文件作有限度的正式改动
senses.example: The council modified the payment clause but left the rest of the contract untouched.
senses.exampleCN: 理事会修改了付款条款，但合同其余部分未动。
senses.why: A legal document is changed clause by clause, never rewritten wholesale if it can be helped. Modify is the natural verb for a bounded edit that leaves the instrument in force.
senses.whyCN: 法律文件是一条款一条款地改，不到万不得已不会整份重写。modify 正是表示这种有限改动、让文件继续有效的动词。

senses.title: Change a setting or file
senses.definition: in computing, to change the contents, settings, or code of a file or system
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机领域，改动文件或系统的内容、设置或代码
senses.example: Do not modify the system files without a backup.
senses.exampleCN: 没有备份时不要修改系统文件。
senses.why: Software is a structure with many settable measures. Editing one setting or one line modifies the system: the rest keeps running, which is exactly the partial-change picture.
senses.whyCN: 软件是一个有许多可调尺度的结构。改一项设置或一行代码就是 modify 系统：其余部分照旧运行，这正是“局部改动”的画面。

senses.title: Rewrite a gene
senses.definition: in biology, to change an organism's genetic material, often to give it a new trait
senses.definitionCN: 在生物学中，改变生物体的遗传物质，常为赋予它新的性状
senses.example: The scientists modified one gene in the rice plant to resist drought.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家改动了水稻的一个基因，使其抗旱。
senses.why: The organism is not replaced; one instruction inside it is re-measured and rewritten. The phrase 'genetically modified' keeps the sense of a targeted edit to an existing living thing.
senses.whyCN: 生物体本身没有被替换，被改写的是它内部的一条指令。“genetically modified”这一说法保留了“对既有生物做定点改动”的意思。

senses.title: Alter a material's surface
senses.definition: in materials science, to change the properties of a surface or structure without changing its bulk
senses.definitionCN: 在材料科学中，改变表面或结构的性能，而不改变其主体
senses.example: The coating modifies the surface without changing the bulk of the metal.
senses.exampleCN: 这层涂层改变了金属的表面性能，却没有改变其主体。
senses.why: Here the measure is applied only to the skin of the object. The bulk stays as it was, which makes modify the right verb for a treatment rather than a replacement.
senses.whyCN: 这里的尺度只施加在物体的表皮上。主体保持原样，因此 modify 适合表示一种处理，而不是替换。

senses.title: A sound changed by its neighbour
senses.titleCN: 语音受邻音影响而变化
senses.definition: in phonetics, of a sound, to be changed under the influence of a neighbouring sound
senses.definitionCN: 在语音学中，指一个音受相邻音影响而发生改变
senses.example: In rapid speech, the final sound is often modified by the sound that follows it.
senses.exampleCN: 在快速语流中，末尾的音常被后面的音改变。
senses.why: A sound keeps its identity but shifts its shape to fit its neighbours, just as a part is trimmed to fit a new pipe. The word's 'fit' sense is at work even here.
senses.whyCN: 一个音保留自己的身份，却改变形状去适应相邻的音，正如一个零件被修整以接上新管道。即便在这里，这个词“适配”的意思仍在起作用。

intro.en: Modify entered English from Old French in the late fourteenth century and goes back to Latin modificare, literally 'to make by measure'. Its two Latin parts, modus and facere, explain why it means partial adjustment rather than total replacement. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: modify 在 14 世纪晚期从古法语进入英语，可追溯到拉丁语 modificare，字面意为“按尺度制作”。它的两个拉丁成分 modus 与 facere，解释了它为何表示局部调整而不是整体替换。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded as modifien, 'alter, amend, adjust, change the properties, form, or function of'. It also meant 'set limits, keep within the bounds of reason; choose a middle course'.
items.cn: 最早记录为 modifien，意为“改变、修正、调整、改变……的性质、形式或功能”。它还有“设定界限、保持在理性范围之内、选择中间道路”的意思。

items.en: The English verb came through Old French modifier (14c.), which already carried the sense of altering something to fit.
items.cn: 这个英语动词经古法语 modifier（14 世纪）而来，后者已经带有“改动某物使其适配”的意思。

items.en: Latin modificare meant 'to limit, measure off, restrain'. It joined modus 'measure, manner' with the combining form of facere 'to make'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 modificare 意为“限定、量出、约束”。它把 modus“尺度、方式”与 facere“制作”的结合形式合在一起。

items.en: Modus goes back to PIE *med- 'take appropriate measures', the root behind mode, moderate, and modest. Facere goes back to PIE *dhe- 'to set, put', the root behind do and deed.
items.cn: modus 可追溯到原始印欧语 *med-“采取恰当的尺度”，也是 mode、moderate、modest 的词根。facere 可追溯到原始印欧语 *dhe-“放置、安放”，也是 do 与 deed 的词根。

items.en: Modification is recorded c. 1500 in philosophy, 'determination by a mode or quality'. Modifier appears in the 1580s as 'one who or that which modifies'; its grammatical sense is from 1865. The 'result of a variation' sense of modification is from the 1660s, and 'act of altering' from 1774.
items.cn: modification 约 1500 年出现在哲学中，意为“由某种模式或性质所决定”。modifier 于 16 世纪 80 年代出现，指“修改者或修改之物”；其语法义始于 1865 年。modification 的“变化结果”义始于 17 世纪 60 年代，“改变的行为”义始于 1774 年。

items.en: Moderate comes from Latin moderari 'keep within measure', the same *med- root but a different branch. Adjust comes from Old French ajouster, from Late Latin adjuxtare 'bring near'. Alter comes from Latin alter 'the other of two'. Each changes something in a different direction or degree.
items.cn: moderate 来自拉丁语 moderari“保持在尺度之内”，同出 *med- 词根，但属于另一分支。adjust 来自古法语 ajouster，源于晚期拉丁语 adjuxtare“使靠近”。alter 来自拉丁语 alter“两者中的另一个”。它们各自以不同方向或不同程度改变事物。

note.en: The first group separates the noun, the agent, and the two participles built on modify; the second compares verbs of change that learners too often use as exact synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组把由 modify 构成的名词、施动者与两个分词分开；第二组比较学习者常当作完全同义词的几个“改变”动词。

entries.definition: a change made to something, or the act of changing it. It names the change or the process, while modify names the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 对某物所作的改动，或改动这一行为。它命名改动或过程，而 modify 命名动作本身。

entries.definition: one who or that which modifies; in grammar, a word that limits another word. It is the doer or the tool, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 修改者或修改之物；语法中指限定另一词的词。它是施动者或工具，不是动作。

entries.definition: changed in some parts, as in 'genetically modified' or 'a modified version'. It describes the result, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 局部被改动的，如“转基因的”或“修改过的版本”。它描述结果，而不是过程。

entries.definition: not changed at all. The un- prefix marks the absence of exactly the partial edit that modify performs.
entries.definitionCN: 完全未被改动的。un- 前缀标记的正是 modify 所做的那种局部改动的缺席。

entries.definition: to change something slightly so that it fits, works, or looks right. It stresses fitting a standard or a position, while modify can also mean changing a design or a rule.
entries.definitionCN: 轻微改变某物，使其合适、正常或位置正确。它强调对准某个标准或位置，而 modify 还可指改动设计或规则。

entries.definition: to make something different, often in a way that changes its character or appearance. It is broader and can suggest a deeper change than modify.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物不同，常指改变其性质或外观。它范围更广，也可能暗示比 modify 更深的改变。

entries.definition: to change a text, law, or agreement in order to correct or improve it. It is mostly formal and textual, whereas modify also covers objects and behaviour.
entries.definitionCN: 为纠正或改进而改动文本、法律或协议。它多用于正式文本，而 modify 也覆盖物件与行为。

entries.definition: to make something less extreme or less intense, or to preside over a discussion. It shares the 'measure' root but works mainly on strength, not on form.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物不那么极端或强烈，或主持讨论。它与 modify 共享“尺度”词根，但主要作用于强度，而不是形式。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Latin modus 'measure' plus facere 'make', and the English family modification, modifier, mode, and moderate.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：拉丁语 modus“尺度”加 facere“制作”，以及英语词族 modification、modifier、mode、moderate。

normal.en: modus is 'measure' and -ify comes from facere 'make'. To modify is to make according to a measure, which is why the thing keeps its identity.
normal.cn: modus 是“尺度”，-ify 来自 facere“制作”。modify 就是按尺度去制作，所以被改的东西保留自己的身份。

normal.en: The Latin verb also meant 'set limits, keep within bounds', so modifying a demand can mean softening it rather than changing its content.
normal.cn: 这个拉丁动词还意为“设定界限、保持在范围之内”，所以修改一项要求可以是把它放缓，而不是改变内容。

normal.en: modification is the change or the act; modifier is the person or word that does it; modified is the result.
normal.cn: modification 是改动或改动行为；modifier 是做这件事的人或词；modified 是结果。

normal.en: mode, moderate, modest and modify all share *med- 'take appropriate measures', but only modify adds the 'make' part.
normal.cn: mode、moderate、modest、modify 都共享 *med-“采取恰当尺度”，但只有 modify 加了“制作”这一部分。

normal.en: In grammar the word narrows meaning: an adjective modifies a noun without replacing it, the same partial-change picture.
normal.cn: 在语法里这个词收窄意义：形容词修饰名词而不替换它，仍是那幅“局部改动”的画面。

abstract.en: Picture a craftsman with a ruler beside an old chair. He shaves one leg, keeps the frame, and the chair is still the same chair.
abstract.cn: 想象一位工匠把尺子放在一把旧椅子旁。他刨短一条腿，保留框架，椅子仍是同一把椅子。

abstract.en: Modify is a dial, not a switch: it turns the value a little, while replace would swap the whole unit out.
abstract.cn: modify 是一个旋钮，不是开关：它把数值稍微转动一点，而 replace 会把整个部件换掉。

abstract.en: Every modified thing still answers to its old name; if it no longer does, it was not modified but replaced.
abstract.cn: 每一件被 modify 的东西仍回应它原来的名字；如果它不再回应，那它不是被修改，而是被替换了。

examples.en: We modified the proposal after the first round of comments.
examples.cn: 第一轮意见之后，我们修改了提案。

examples.en: The app lets you modify the layout without changing the underlying data.
examples.cn: 这个应用允许你修改布局，而不改动底层数据。

examples.en: Some crops were modified to grow in salt water, but the yield remains low.
examples.cn: 有些作物被改造为能在咸水中生长，但产量仍然很低。

dict_mnemonic.text: “摸得改”——先摸清原有尺寸，再动手改那几处，整体不换 → modify 修改、调整（只借音，不表词源）

root: 源自拉丁语 modificare“按尺度制作”，由 modus“尺度”加 facere“制作”构成，核心是“按尺寸修整局部，而不整体替换”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of modify, all from one gesture: a measure is laid on an existing thing and a few parts are trimmed, while the thing itself remains what it was.
sensesIntro.cn: modify 的九个义项都来自同一个动作：把尺子放在既有之物上，修整其中几处，而物件本身仍是原来的物件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a few parts trimmed to measure, the whole left standing.
core.cn: 核心意象：按尺寸修整几处，整体仍然立着。

branches.en: PARTIAL CHANGE: details or parts are re-measured, either to improve the thing or to fit a new use.
branches.cn: 局部改变：细节或部件被重新量过，或为改良物件，或为适配新用途。

branches.en: GRAMMAR: a word places a measure on another word and narrows its meaning without replacing it.
branches.cn: 语法：一个词给另一个词加上尺度，收窄它的意义，而不替换它。

branches.en: BOUNDS AND TEXT: a tone or demand is brought back inside measure, and a legal clause is edited while the document stays in force.
branches.cn: 尺度与文本：语气或要求被拉回尺度之内，法律条款被改动而文件继续有效。

branches.en: SYSTEMS AND GENES: one setting, one line of code, or one gene is changed while the rest keeps running.
branches.cn: 系统与基因：一项设置、一行代码或一个基因被改动，其余部分照旧运行。

branches.en: SURFACE AND SOUND: only the skin of a material, or the shape of a sound, is adjusted to fit its surroundings.
branches.cn: 表面与语音：只调整材料的表皮或一个音的形状，使其适应周围环境。

intro.en: Modify is a Latin verb whose English shape joins mod- 'measure' to -ify 'make'. The same stem, with -ation, -er, -ed, -able and un-, produces the rest of the family.
intro.cn: modify 是拉丁语动词，其英语形态把 mod-“尺度”与 -ify“制作”合在一起。同一词干加上 -ation、-er、-ed、-able 与 un-，构成其余词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin modificare combined modus 'measure' and facere 'make'. Facere also gives -fic-, -fect, and -fy in English, which is why modify, manufacture, and effect all contain a 'making' piece.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 modificare 把 modus“尺度”与 facere“制作”合起来。facere 在英语里还给出 -fic-、-fect 与 -fy，所以 modify、manufacture、effect 都含有一个“制作”的成分。

items.meaning: to make according to measure; to change in part
items.meaningCN: 按尺度制作；局部改变（mod- 尺度 + -ify 使……）
items.example: They modified the engine to burn less fuel.
items.exampleCN: 他们改动了发动机，使其更省油。

items.meaning: a change, or the act of changing
items.meaningCN: 修改；改动（-ation 构成行为名词）
items.example: The design needs only a small modification.
items.exampleCN: 这个设计只需要做一处小改动。

items.meaning: one who modifies; a grammatical qualifier
items.meaningCN: 修改者；修饰语（-er 表施动者）
items.example: In the phrase 'very cold', 'very' is a modifier.
items.exampleCN: 在 very cold 这一短语中，very 是修饰语。

items.meaningCN: 被局部改动的（-ed 构成过去分词）
items.exampleCN: 修改后的版本运行得更快。

items.meaningCN: 未修改的（un- 否定 + modified）
items.example: The control group used unmodified seed.
items.exampleCN: 对照组使用的是未经改造的种子。

items.example: The settings are modifiable by the user.
items.exampleCN: 这些设置可由用户修改。

items.meaning: a user-made change to a game
items.meaningCN: 模组；游戏修改版（modification 的截短）
items.example: He installed a mod that adds new maps.
items.exampleCN: 他安装了一个增加新地图的模组。

items.example: The device has a low-power mode.
items.exampleCN: 这个设备有一个低功耗模式。

items.meaning: kept within measure; to reduce intensity
items.meaningCN: 适度的；使缓和（保持在尺度内）
items.example: She moderated her criticism in public.
items.exampleCN: 她在公开场合缓和了自己的批评。

items.meaning: a person's usual way of working
items.meaningCN: 一贯做法；做事方式（拉丁语“工作的方式”）
items.example: The thief's modus operandi was always the same.
items.exampleCN: 这个窃贼的作案手法始终如一。

items.meaning: to treat something as a commodity
items.meaningCN: 使商品化（com- 共同 + mod- 尺度 + -ify 使……）
items.example: Critics say the festival has commodified local music.
items.exampleCN: 批评者说这个节日把本地音乐商品化了。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 限定；量出；约束（modus 尺度 + facere 制作）

definition_zh: n. 未婚男子；单身汉；学士（学位）；（旧时）年轻骑士
definition_en: An unmarried man; a first university degree; historically, a young knight without a following.
core_image: 一个人吃饭一个人住的那张桌子
scene: 他四十岁仍是单身，桌上摊着学士学位证书。 He was still a bachelor at forty, his degree certificate spread on the table.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：bachelor 指从未结婚的成年男子。

pos.zh: 未婚男子；学士；年轻骑士

senses.title: An unmarried man
senses.definition: a man who has never married, especially one living alone
senses.definitionCN: 从未结婚的男子，尤指独居者
senses.example: He lived as a bachelor for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他过了三十年单身生活。
senses.why: The word named a young man without land or a household of his own, so the unmarried sense came first.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原指没有土地也没有自己家室的年轻人，因此未婚义最先出现。

senses.title: A first university degree
senses.definition: the first degree awarded by a university, below a master and a doctor
senses.definitionCN: 大学授予的第一级学位，低于硕士与博士
senses.example: She holds a bachelor of science in biology.
senses.exampleCN: 她持有生物学理学士学位。
senses.why: Universities borrowed the knightly rank for their lowest grade, so a student became a bachelor before a master.
senses.whyCN: 大学把骑士等级借用为最低学阶，于是学生先成 bachelor 再成 master。

senses.title: A young knight
senses.definition: in medieval use, a knight too young or too poor to lead his own followers
senses.definitionCN: 在中世纪用法中，指太年轻或太穷而无法自带随从的骑士
senses.example: The knight bachelor rode without a banner.
senses.exampleCN: 那位下级骑士出行不带旗号。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, and it explains the other two: a man not yet head of anything.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，也解释了另外两个：一个尚未成为任何事物之首的男人。

intro.en: Bachelor comes from Old French bacheler, a young man or aspirant knight, from Medieval Latin baccalaris, whose origin is uncertain but may mean a farm hand.
intro.cn: bachelor 来自古法语 bacheler「年轻人、见习骑士」，出自中世纪拉丁语 baccalaris，其来源不确定，可能意为「农庄雇工」。

items.en: Baccalaris named a young man of low rank, possibly a worker on a farm estate.
items.cn: baccalaris 指地位较低的年轻人，可能是农庄上的雇工。

items.en: Old French bacheler meant a young man training to be a knight.
items.cn: 古法语 bacheler 意为「受训成为骑士的年轻人」。

items.en: Middle English took the word for a young knight without his own banner.
items.cn: 中古英语借入该词，指没有自己旗号的下级骑士。

items.en: Universities used it for the first degree, below master and doctor.
items.cn: 大学用它指第一级学位，低于硕士与博士。

items.en: The same century fixed the sense of a man who has never married.
items.cn: 同一个世纪确立了「从未结婚的男子」这一义项。

items.en: The spelling settled as bachelor, while baccalaureate kept a learned Latin look.
items.cn: 拼法定为 bachelor，而 baccalaureate 保留了学术味的拉丁外观。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the degree family; the near-meaning group lists words for people who are not married.
note.cn: 形近组保留学位词族；近义组列出表示未婚者的词。

entries.definition: A first degree or school-leaving exam.
entries.definitionCN: 学士学位或中学毕业会考。

entries.definition: An unmarried woman.
entries.definitionCN: 未婚女子。

entries.definition: A member of a council.
entries.definitionCN: 议会成员。

entries.definition: A head of state or university.
entries.definitionCN: 总理；大学名誉校长。

entries.definition: Not married or in a relationship.
entries.definitionCN: 未婚或无伴侣的。

entries.definition: An unmarried woman, in older use.
entries.definitionCN: 旧用法中的未婚女子。

entries.definition: Abstaining from marriage by choice.
entries.definitionCN: 自愿不婚的。

entries.definition: A person who holds a degree.
entries.definitionCN: 持有学位的人。

normalIntro.en: Bachelor began as a young knight with no followers, so it came to mean a man with no household and then the lowest degree.
normalIntro.cn: bachelor 起初指没有随从的年轻骑士，于是转指没有家室的男子，再指最低一级学位。

normal.en: The degree phrase takes an apostrophe s.
normal.cn: 学位短语要加撇号 s。

normal.en: Bachelor of Arts and of Science are the pair.
normal.cn: 文学学士与理学士是一对。

normal.en: A confirmed bachelor will not marry.
normal.cn: 铁心单身汉指不打算结婚的人。

normal.en: Bachelorhood is the state, bachelor the man.
normal.cn: bachelorhood 是状态，bachelor 是人。

normal.en: Knight bachelor is the old rank.
normal.cn: knight bachelor 是旧时等级。

abstract.en: Picture a table laid for one.
abstract.cn: 想象一张只摆一人份的餐桌。

abstract.en: Imagine a rider with no banner behind him.
abstract.cn: 想象一名身后无旗的骑手。

abstract.en: Think of the first rung of a ladder.
abstract.cn: 想象梯子的第一级。

examples.en: He remained a bachelor all his life.
examples.cn: 他一生未婚。

examples.en: She finished her bachelor of engineering.
examples.cn: 她读完了工学学士。

examples.en: They rented a small bachelor flat.
examples.cn: 他们租了一间小的单身公寓。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音记忆：读作「拜了个了」——把婚事拜别了结，一个人过，就是 bachelor 单身汉；学位义则是学阶里的「第一级」。

root: 中世纪拉丁语 baccalaris「低位年轻人」经古法语 bacheler「见习骑士」入英语；因指「尚未成家立业者」，衍生出未婚男子与大学第一级学位两义。

sensesIntro.en: All three senses describe a man not yet head of anything: no banner, no household, and no higher degree.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项都在描述一个尚未成为任何事物之首的男人：没有旗号、没有家室、没有更高学位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a table laid for one person only
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人吃饭一个人住的那张桌子

branches.en: A man of forty living alone.
branches.cn: 四十岁独居的男子。

branches.en: Thirty years without a marriage.
branches.cn: 三十年未曾结婚。

branches.en: A first degree in biology.
branches.cn: 生物学的第一级学位。

branches.en: A knight riding without a banner.
branches.cn: 不带旗号出行的骑士。

branches.en: Both name a man without a following.
branches.cn: 两者都指没有随从的人。

intro.en: Bachelor is a single French root with the agent ending -or; -ette marks the female form and -hood the state.
intro.cn: bachelor 是一个法语词根加施事词尾 -or；-ette 标记女性形式，-hood 标记状态。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is baccalaris, a young man of low rank; Latin bacca, berry, was later imagined inside baccalaureate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 baccalaris「低位年轻人」；后来人们又把拉丁语 bacca「浆果」附会进 baccalaureate。

definition_zh: n. 唤起，激起（兴趣、情绪、注意）；（生理与心理学）唤醒状态，兴奋水平
definition_en: The act of stirring a feeling, interest or response into activity; in psychology and physiology, the level of alertness and activation of the body.
core_image: 把睡着的那根弦一下拨响
scene: 咖啡因提高了警觉与生理唤醒水平。 Caffeine raises alertness and physiological arousal.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：在心理学与生理学中，arousal 指身体的唤醒与激活水平。

senses.title: Stirring a feeling into activity
senses.definition: the act of waking interest, anger, curiosity or desire so that it becomes active
senses.definitionCN: 把兴趣、愤怒、好奇或欲望唤醒，使之变为活跃状态的行为
senses.example: The photograph caused widespread arousal of public anger.
senses.exampleCN: 那张照片激起了公众普遍的愤怒。
senses.why: The verb arouse meant to shake a bird into flight, so the noun keeps that sudden start from stillness.
senses.whyCN: 动词 arouse 原意是把鸟惊飞，所以这个名词保留着「从静止中猛然启动」的画面。

senses.title: The body's activation level
senses.definition: in psychology and physiology, a measurable state of alertness ranging from deep sleep to high excitement
senses.definitionCN: 在心理学与生理学中，指从深睡到高度兴奋之间可测量的警觉状态
senses.example: Performance drops when arousal is either too low or too high.
senses.exampleCN: 唤醒水平过低或过高，表现都会下降。
senses.why: Science needed a neutral word for how switched on the body is, and arousal supplied it without judging the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 科学需要一个中性词来描述身体「开机」的程度，arousal 恰好胜任，且不对感受作评价。

intro.en: Arousal is arouse plus the action suffix -al. Rouse comes from Middle English rousen, to shake, originally a falconry term for making a hawk stir its feathers.
intro.cn: arousal 是 arouse 加动作名词后缀 -al。rouse 来自中古英语 rousen「抖动」，原本是鹰猎术语，指让鹰抖动羽毛。

items.en: Middle English rousen meant to shake or startle, used of birds and of sleeping people alike.
items.cn: 中古英语 rousen 意为「抖动、惊动」，既用于鸟，也用于睡着的人。

items.en: In falconry a hawk was roused when it shook its feathers and became alert, the image behind the whole family.
items.cn: 鹰猎中，鹰抖动羽毛转为警觉称为 roused，这是整个词族背后的画面。

items.en: English added the intensive prefix a- to give arouse, to stir up thoroughly, by the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪，英语加上强调前缀 a- 得到 arouse，意为「彻底激起」。

items.en: The action noun arousal is recorded in 1849, formed with -al as in arrival and refusal.
items.cn: 动作名词 arousal 记录于 1849 年，用 -al 构成，与 arrival、refusal 同型。

items.en: Early twentieth-century psychology adopted arousal for the body's activation level, giving arousal theory.
items.cn: 20 世纪初心理学采用 arousal 指身体激活水平，产生了唤醒理论。

items.en: Today arousal is standard in sleep research, emotion studies and sports science.
items.cn: 如今 arousal 是睡眠研究、情绪研究与运动科学的标准用语。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against carousal, a noisy drinking party, which differs by one letter; the near-meaning group lists words for being stirred up.
note.cn: 形近组提醒别与只差一个字母的 carousal「喧闹酒宴」混淆；近义组列出表示被激起的词。

entries.definition: To stir a feeling into activity.
entries.definitionCN: 把感情激起。

entries.definition: To wake or startle someone.
entries.definitionCN: 唤醒或惊动某人。

entries.definition: A noisy drinking party.
entries.definitionCN: 喧闹的饮酒聚会。

entries.definition: The act of reaching a place.
entries.definitionCN: 到达某地这一行为。

entries.definition: A stirred-up, eager state.
entries.definitionCN: 被激起的急切状态。

entries.definition: Something that prompts activity.
entries.definitionCN: 促使活动的刺激。

entries.definition: The act of becoming aware.
entries.definitionCN: 开始察觉的过程。

entries.definition: The state of being watchful.
entries.definitionCN: 警觉的状态。

normalIntro.en: Arousal is arouse plus -al: the act of stirring something awake, from a sleeping hawk to a whole nervous system.
normalIntro.cn: arousal 就是 arouse 加 -al：把某物搅醒这件事，从一只睡着的鹰到整个神经系统。

normal.en: It is uncountable: say high arousal, not an arousal.
normal.cn: 它不可数：说 high arousal，不说 an arousal。

normal.en: Arousal is the noun; arouse is the verb.
normal.cn: arousal 是名词，arouse 是动词。

normal.en: Do not confuse arousal with carousal, a drinking party.
normal.cn: 别把 arousal 与 carousal「酒宴」混淆。

normal.en: Arousal level is the fixed term in psychology.
normal.cn: arousal level 是心理学固定术语。

normal.en: The -al ending matches arrival and refusal.
normal.cn: -al 词尾与 arrival、refusal 同型。

abstract.en: Picture a hawk shaking its feathers awake.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鹰抖羽转醒。

abstract.en: Imagine a slack string suddenly plucked.
abstract.cn: 想象一根松弦被猛然拨响。

abstract.en: Think of a dial turned from sleep to alert.
abstract.cn: 想象一个从睡眠拧到警觉的旋钮。

examples.en: The drug reduces arousal and helps sleep.
examples.cn: 这种药降低唤醒水平，帮助入睡。

examples.en: Loud noise produces measurable arousal.
examples.cn: 巨大声响会引起可测量的唤醒。

examples.en: The film relies on shock rather than arousal of interest.
examples.cn: 这部电影靠惊吓，而不是靠唤起兴趣。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：arouse「唤起」+ -al「动作名词」——唤起这件事本身，就是 arousal。

root: 中古英语 rousen「抖动、惊起」原为鹰猎用语，加强调前缀 a- 成 arouse「彻底激起」，1849 年再加动作后缀 -al 构成 arousal；20 世纪心理学用它指唤醒水平。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one waking: a feeling stirred into activity, and the same stirring measured as the body's activation level.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一次「醒来」：感情被激起而活跃，以及同一种激起被测量为身体的激活水平。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one slack string suddenly plucked into sound
core.cn: 核心意象：把睡着的那根弦一下拨响

branches.en: A photograph stirring public anger.
branches.cn: 激起公众愤怒的照片。

branches.en: Curiosity woken by a strange noise.
branches.cn: 被怪声唤醒的好奇。

branches.en: A dial from deep sleep to alert.
branches.cn: 从深睡到警觉的旋钮。

branches.en: Performance falling at both extremes.
branches.cn: 两端都下滑的表现。

branches.en: Both name the move out of stillness.
branches.cn: 两者都指从静止中启动。

intro.en: Arousal is the prefix a- plus rouse plus -al; the same -al builds arrival, refusal and proposal.
intro.cn: arousal 是前缀 a- 加 rouse 加 -al；同一 -al 还构成 arrival、refusal 与 proposal。

latinIntro.en: Rouse itself is not Latin, so the classical layer belongs to its synonyms: excitare, to stir up, and stimulus, a goad.
latinIntro.cn: rouse 本身不是拉丁词，所以古典层次属于它的近义词：excitare「激起」与 stimulus「刺棒」。

definition_zh: v. 宣告（婚姻、合同等）无效；废除；取消
definition_en: To declare a marriage, contract or official act legally void, as if it had never existed.
core_image: 把那份文件从头到尾划掉，当作没发生过
scene: 法院认定这段婚姻自始就不成立。 The court agreed to annul the marriage.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：annul 不是「离婚」，而是宣告这段婚姻自始无效，法律上当作从未存在。

forms.label: 过去式与过去分词（双写 l）

senses.title: To declare legally void
senses.definition: to rule that a marriage or contract never had legal force, so it is treated as never having existed
senses.definitionCN: 裁定某段婚姻或合同从未具有法律效力，因而视为从未存在
senses.example: They sought to annul the marriage on grounds of fraud.
senses.exampleCN: 他们以欺诈为由申请宣告婚姻无效。
senses.why: Latin nullus means not any, so annul literally makes a thing into nothing: the record is not ended but erased from the start.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 nullus 意为「没有任何一个」，所以 annul 字面上是把某物变成「无」：记录不是被终止，而是从头被抹去。

senses.title: To cancel or abolish generally
senses.titleCN: 一般意义上的取消或废除
senses.definition: to cancel an act, result or arrangement so that it no longer counts
senses.definitionCN: 取消某项行为、结果或安排，使其不再生效
senses.example: The board voted to annul the earlier resolution.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会投票撤销先前的决议。
senses.why: Outside strict law the word keeps the same zeroing image, but the erasure is practical rather than retroactive.
senses.whyCN: 在严格法律之外，该词保留同一幅「归零」画面，只是抹除是实际层面的，而非追溯性的。

intro.en: Annul is Late Latin annullare, from ad-, to, and nullus, not any, from ne-, not, and ullus, any. The word literally means to reduce to nothing.
intro.cn: annul 来自晚期拉丁语 annullare，由 ad-「向」与 nullus「没有任何一个」构成，而 nullus 又由 ne-「不」与 ullus「任何」组成。这个词字面意为「使归于无」。

items.en: Latin nullus meant not any, built from ne-, not, and ullus, any. It gives null, nullify, nullity and annihilate.
items.cn: 拉丁语 nullus 意为「没有任何一个」，由 ne-「不」与 ullus「任何」构成。它产生 null、nullify、nullity 与 annihilate。

items.en: The prefix ad- assimilates to an- before n, which produces the double n and distinguishes annul from annual.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 在 n 前同化为 an-，形成双写 n，也把 annul 与 annual 区分开。

items.en: Annullare meant to reduce to nothing, and was used in church law for declaring a marriage void from the beginning.
items.cn: annullare 意为「使归于无」，在教会法中用于宣告婚姻自始无效。

items.en: Old French annuller passed the verb into Middle English in the fifteenth century, keeping the legal sense.
items.cn: 古法语 annuller 在 15 世纪把该动词传入中古英语，保留法律义。

items.en: Modern English doubles the l before -ed and -ing, and the noun annulment is the standard term in family law.
items.cn: 现代英语在 -ed 与 -ing 前双写 l，名词 annulment 是家事法中的标准术语。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against annual, about years; the near-meaning group lists other words for cancelling legal force.
note.cn: 形近组提醒别与 annual「每年的」混淆；近义组列出其他表示取消法律效力的词。

entries.definition: The act of declaring void.
entries.definitionCN: 宣告无效的行为。

entries.definition: Having no legal force; zero.
entries.definitionCN: 无法律效力的；零的。

entries.definition: To make legally void or ineffective.
entries.definitionCN: 使法律上无效或失效。

entries.definition: Happening once a year.
entries.definitionCN: 每年一次的。

entries.definition: To call off something planned.
entries.definitionCN: 取消已计划之事。

entries.definition: To withdraw a licence or order.
entries.definitionCN: 撤回许可或命令。

entries.definition: To make legally invalid.
entries.definitionCN: 使法律上无效。

entries.definition: To cancel a contract or rule.
entries.definitionCN: 取消合同或规则。

normalIntro.en: Annul is an- plus null: reduce to nothing, so the act is treated as never having happened.
normalIntro.cn: annul 就是 an- 加 null：使归于无，所以那件事被当作从未发生。

normal.en: Double the l: annulled, annulling, but annuls.
normal.cn: 双写 l：annulled、annulling，但 annuls。

normal.en: Annulment erases from the start; divorce ends a valid marriage.
normal.cn: annulment 从头抹去，divorce 结束一段有效婚姻。

normal.en: Do not confuse annul with annual, about years.
normal.cn: 别把 annul 与 annual「每年的」混淆。

normal.en: The noun is annulment, not annulation.
normal.cn: 名词是 annulment，不是 annulation。

normal.en: Null and void is the fixed legal pair.
normal.cn: null and void 是固定法律搭配。

abstract.en: Picture a document crossed out from the first line to the last.
abstract.cn: 想象一份文件从第一行到最后一行被划掉。

abstract.en: Imagine a record that is removed rather than closed.
abstract.cn: 想象一份被移除而非被封存的记录。

abstract.en: Think of a number reset to zero instead of counted down.
abstract.cn: 想象一个被重置为零而非倒数的数字。

examples.en: The court will annul the contract if fraud is proved.
examples.cn: 若证实欺诈，法院将宣告合同无效。

examples.en: They applied to annul the marriage after two months.
examples.cn: 两个月后他们申请宣告婚姻无效。

examples.en: The committee annulled the result and ordered a recount.
examples.cn: 委员会宣布结果无效并下令重新计票。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：an「向」+ nul「零、无」——把一份文件推向「零」，当作从未存在，就是宣告无效 annul。

root: 拉丁语 ne-「不」+ ullus「任何」构成 nullus「没有任何一个」，加 ad- 成 annullare「使归于无」，经古法语 annuller 入英语为 annul，指宣告自始无效。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one zeroing: the strict legal erasure of a marriage or contract, and the everyday cancelling of a decision.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一次归零：严格法律上对婚姻或合同的抹除，以及日常对一项决定的取消。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a document struck through as if it never existed
core.cn: 核心意象：一份被划掉、当作从未存在的文件

branches.en: A marriage erased from the register.
branches.cn: 一段从登记册上抹去的婚姻。

branches.en: A contract void from the first day.
branches.cn: 一份自第一天起就无效的合同。

branches.en: A resolution struck from the minutes.
branches.cn: 一项从会议记录中删去的决议。

branches.en: An election result set aside.
branches.cn: 一个被搁置的选举结果。

branches.en: Both turn something into nothing.
branches.cn: 两者都把某物变成无。

intro.en: Annul is ad- plus null, and the null root builds nullify, nullity and annihilate.
intro.cn: annul 是 ad- 加 null，null 词根还构成 nullify、nullity 与 annihilate。

latinIntro.en: Latin nullus is ne-, not, plus ullus, any; adding ad- gives annullare, to reduce to nothing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 nullus 由 ne-「不」加 ullus「任何」构成；加上 ad- 得到 annullare「使归于无」。

latinEntries.exampleCN: nullus 产生 null 与 annul。

latinEntries.example: Ullus is the second half of nullus.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ullus 是 nullus 的后半部分。

definition_zh: 诱惑力；魅力；（动词）诱惑；吸引
definition_en: the power of something to attract or fascinate, especially by promising pleasure or advantage; as a verb, to attract or tempt
core_image: 钓钩上那点闪光，让人忍不住伸手
scene: 那份工作薪水一般，却承诺三年后能独立带队。 The allure of running his own team won him over.
sceneCN: 这里 allure 是「诱惑力」（第 1 个义项：让人向往、忍不住被吸引的魅力）；句意为「能自己带队」这一点打动了他。核心画面是钓钩上那点闪光，让人忍不住伸手。

forms.label: 过去式与过去分词（动词）

derivatives.zh: 现在分词作形容词，义为「诱人的；迷人的」
加 -ly 构成，义为「诱人地」
加 -ment 构成，义为「诱惑；诱惑物」

senses.title: The quality that draws you in
senses.definition: the power of something to attract or fascinate, especially by promising pleasure or advantage
senses.definitionCN: 某物吸引或令人着迷的力量，尤指通过承诺快乐或好处
senses.example: The allure of the open road kept him travelling.
senses.exampleCN: 开阔公路的魅力让他一直在路上。
senses.why: Allure comes from a- plus lure, a bait, so the word keeps the fishing picture: something shiny dangles and you move toward it.
senses.whyCN: allure 来自 a- 加 lure「饵」，所以该词保留了钓鱼的画面：有个闪光的东西悬在那里，你就朝它移动。

senses.title: To attract by temptation
senses.definition: to attract or tempt someone, often by offering something desirable, the older verbal use of the word
senses.definitionCN: 吸引或引诱某人，常通过提供令人向往的东西，是该词较早的动词用法
senses.example: The brochure allured them with images of empty beaches.
senses.exampleCN: 这本手册用空无一人的海滩图片吸引他们。
senses.why: Here the bait is actively thrown: the subject does the luring rather than merely possessing the charm.
senses.whyCN: 这里饵是被主动抛出的：主语在「下饵」，而不只是拥有那种魅力。

intro.en: Allure is a- plus lure: the Old French loirre, a falconer bait, gave lure, and English added a- to make both a verb and a noun of attraction.
intro.cn: allure 是 a- 加 lure：古法语 loirre「驯鹰人的诱饵」产生 lure，英语加上 a-，造出表示吸引的动词与名词。

items.en: Old French loirre meant a falconer bait, a piece of meat used to call a hawk back to the fist.
items.cn: 古法语 loirre 指驯鹰人的诱饵，即用来把猎鹰唤回拳头上的一块肉。

items.en: The verb aloirer meant to attract with a bait, built from a-, to, plus loirre.
items.cn: 动词 aloirer 意为「用饵吸引」，由 a-「向」加 loirre 构成。

items.en: Middle English aluren meant to tempt or attract, and the noun alure named the power of attraction.
items.cn: 中古英语 aluren 意为引诱或吸引，名词 alure 指吸引力。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the spelling settled as allure, used of both the charm and the act of charming.
items.cn: 到十六世纪拼写固定为 allure，既指魅力，也指施展魅力的动作。

items.en: Modern use favours the noun, with alluring as the common adjective and the verb now rather literary.
items.cn: 现代用法偏重名词，alluring 是常见形容词，动词如今颇具书面色彩。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the lure family and similar openings; the near-meaning group lists other words for attraction.
note.cn: 形近组保留 lure 词族与相近开头；近义组列出其他表示「吸引」的词。

entries.definition: A bait used to attract.
entries.definitionCN: 用来吸引的诱饵。

entries.definition: Strongly attractive or tempting.
entries.definitionCN: 极具吸引力或诱惑力的。

entries.definition: The act of tempting, or a temptation.
entries.definitionCN: 诱惑的行为，或诱惑物。

entries.definition: To refer to something indirectly.
entries.definitionCN: 间接提及某事。

entries.definition: The power to please and attract.
entries.definitionCN: 令人愉悦并吸引人的力量。

entries.definition: The quality of being attractive.
entries.definitionCN: 具有吸引力的性质。

entries.definition: A powerful hold on the attention.
entries.definitionCN: 对注意力的强烈吸引。

entries.definition: Something that draws you toward a want.
entries.definitionCN: 把你拉向某种欲望的东西。

normalIntro.en: Allure is a- plus lure: a bait held out, and the pull you feel toward it.
normalIntro.cn: allure 就是 a- 加 lure：伸出去的饵，以及你感到的那股拉力。

normal.en: Lure is hidden inside allure, so always picture a fishing hook with something shiny.
normal.cn: allure 里面藏着 lure，所以永远想象一个挂着闪光物的钓钩。

normal.en: The noun is usually uncountable: the allure of fame, not an allure.
normal.cn: 名词通常不可数：the allure of fame，不说 an allure。

normal.en: The fixed phrase is the allure of something, with of, not for.
normal.cn: 固定搭配是 the allure of something，用 of，不用 for。

normal.en: Alluring is the everyday adjective; the verb allure sounds literary.
normal.cn: alluring 是日常形容词，动词 allure 听起来很书面。

normal.en: Do not confuse allure with allude: one attracts, the other hints.
normal.cn: 别把 allure 与 allude 混淆：一个是吸引，一个是暗示。

abstract.en: Picture a bright feather drifting just above the water.
abstract.cn: 想象一片亮羽毛在水面上方轻轻飘动。

abstract.en: Imagine a shop window that makes you stop without deciding to.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇橱窗，让你不由自主地停下脚步。

abstract.en: Think of a promise hanging at the end of a thin line.
abstract.cn: 想象一个承诺悬在一根细线的末端。

examples.en: The allure of quick money blinded him to the risk.
examples.cn: 快钱的诱惑让他看不见风险。

examples.en: The old town has lost none of its allure.
examples.cn: 这座老城丝毫未减它的魅力。

examples.en: They were allured by the promise of free land.
examples.cn: 他们被免费土地的承诺所吸引。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「阿路尔」——阿（a）路（l）尔（lure）：路上挂着饵，把你一路引过去，就是诱惑力、魅力。

root: 古法语 loirre「驯鹰人的诱饵」加前缀 a- 构成 aloirer「用饵吸引」，经中古英语 aluren 演变为 allure，名词指吸引力，动词指引诱，字面即「把饵伸向你」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one bait seen from two sides: the noun names the pull you feel, and the verb names the act of holding out something that pulls.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一个饵的两面：名词指你感到的那股拉力，动词指把会拉人的东西伸出去这个动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shiny bait that makes you reach out
core.cn: 核心意象：一点闪光的饵让你忍不住伸手

branches.en: Fame glittering at a distance.
branches.cn: 名声在远处闪光。

branches.en: A city that promises a new life.
branches.cn: 一座承诺新生活的城市。

branches.en: A brochure holding out empty beaches.
branches.cn: 一本手册伸出空无一人的海滩。

branches.en: A recruiter dangling a promotion.
branches.cn: 招聘者悬着一个升职机会。

branches.en: Both work by holding out a bait.
branches.cn: 两者都靠伸出诱饵起作用。

intro.en: Allure is a- plus lure, and from that bait come alluring, allurement and the plain verb lure itself.
intro.cn: allure 是 a- 加 lure，从这个「饵」派生出 alluring、allurement 以及动词 lure 本身。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin layer: it came from Old French loirre, a falconer bait of Germanic origin, with the prefix a- added in French.
latinIntro.cn: 该词没有拉丁语层次：它来自古法语 loirre「驯鹰人的诱饵」，源于日耳曼语，前缀 a- 是在法语中加上的。

latinEntries.exampleCN: aloirer 是 allure 的来源。

definition_zh: 违反（法律、规则）；违背（协议、誓言）；侵犯（权利、隐私）；亵渎（圣地）；强暴；（体育）犯规；侵入（领地、领空）
definition_en: the act of breaking or acting against a law, a rule, an agreement, a right or something held sacred
core_image: 一道刷在地上的红线被人一脚踏过，线外立着写有禁止字样的木牌，脚印清晰地留在另一侧
scene: 环保督察在保护区里发现一片被砍倒的树木，当场按森林保护条例开出违法通知单。 After finding the felled trees inside the reserve, the inspector issued a citation for violation of the forest code.
sceneCN: 这里指「对法规的违反」，对应第 1 个义项：以作为或不作为破坏法律规定的行为；句意为督察在保护区内发现被砍的树木后，依森林保护条例开出违法通知单。画面要点：红线、禁止木牌、留在另一侧的脚印。

pos.zh: 违反；违背；侵犯；亵渎（可数，常与 of 连用指出被破坏的对象）
（一次具体的）违法行为；违规事例（可数，警察与法庭文书常用）
（体育中的）犯规（可数，裁判用语）

derivatives.zh: 去掉名词后缀后的动词原形，回到拉丁 violare「以强力对待」→ 由「施加强力」转为「破坏、触犯」
violate 加施事后缀（源自拉丁语，表做某事的人）→ 由「违反」这一动作转为「违反者、侵害者」
violate 加形容词后缀（源自拉丁语，表倾向）→ 由「违反」转为「构成违反的、侵害性的」
加否定前缀与表「能够被……」的形容词后缀→ 由「可被侵犯」转为「不可侵犯的、神圣不可破的」
加否定前缀于拉丁分词 violatus → 由「已被破坏」转为「完好未损的、未被亵渎的」

senses.title: The breaking of a law
senses.definition: an act that breaks a statute or an ordinance, or the fact of breaking it
senses.definitionCN: 破坏成文法或法令的行为，或这种破坏本身
senses.example: After finding the felled trees inside the reserve, the inspector issued a notice for violation of the forest code.
senses.exampleCN: 在保护区内发现被砍的树木后，督察依森林保护条例开出违法通知。
senses.why: Latin violare meant to treat something with force, and a statute is treated with force when someone acts straight through it; the noun violation names that act of forcing past a legal line.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 violare 意为「以强力对待」，当有人径直穿过法条行事，就是对该法条施加强力；名词 violation 指这种强行越过法律界线的行为。

senses.title: The breach of a rule or regulation
senses.definition: the failure to obey a rule, code or administrative regulation that is not itself a criminal statute
senses.definitionCN: 未遵守某项规则、守则或行政条例，而该规则本身并非刑事法律
senses.example: Parking on the grass is a violation of the club's rules.
senses.exampleCN: 把车停在草地上违反了俱乐部的规定。
senses.why: The force need not be aimed at a state; a club, a school or an agency draws its own line, and forcing past it produces the same noun on a smaller scale.
senses.whyCN: 这股强力不必冲着国家而去；俱乐部、学校或机构也会自画界线，强行越过就在更小的尺度上产生同一个名词。

senses.title: The breaking of an agreement
senses.definition: the failure to honour a contract, treaty or promise that binds two parties
senses.definitionCN: 未履行约束双方的合同、条约或承诺
senses.example: The company was sued for violation of the supply contract.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司因违反供货合同而被起诉。
senses.why: A contract is a line two parties drew together; forcing through it is the same physical gesture, except the injured party is the partner rather than the state.
senses.whyCN: 合同是双方共同画下的一条线；强行穿过去是同一个动作，只是受损方由国家变成了合作方。

senses.title: The infringement of a right
senses.definition: an interference with someone's legal right, privacy or personal freedom
senses.definitionCN: 对他人法定权利、隐私或个人自由的干涉
senses.example: Reading her letters without permission was a violation of her privacy.
senses.exampleCN: 未经允许拆看她的信件侵犯了她的隐私。
senses.why: A right is a boundary drawn around a person; the force now presses into someone's own space, so the act is felt as invasion rather than mere non-compliance.
senses.whyCN: 权利是画在一个人周围的界线；此时强力压进的是某人自己的空间，于是这一行为被感受为侵入，而不只是不合规。

senses.title: The desecration of something sacred
senses.definition: the treatment of a sacred place, object or rite with irreverence or destructive force
senses.definitionCN: 以不敬或破坏性的强力对待圣地、圣物或仪式
senses.example: Digging up the burial ground was condemned as a violation of the dead.
senses.exampleCN: 挖掘那片墓地受到谴责，被视为对逝者的亵渎。
senses.why: The oldest lines were drawn by religion, and violare in Roman usage already covered the dishonouring of temples; the noun keeps that sacred sense alongside its legal one.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的界线由宗教画出，violare 在罗马用法中本就涵盖对神庙的污损；这个名词因此与法律义并行地保留了神圣义。

senses.title: Sexual assault, in formal and legal use
senses.titleCN: 正式与法律语境中的强暴
senses.definition: the crime of forcing sexual contact on a person against their will, phrased in formal or legal registers
senses.definitionCN: 违背他人意愿强行施加性接触的罪行，用于正式或法律语体
senses.example: The statute treats such a violation as a felony.
senses.exampleCN: 该法将此类强暴行为定为重罪。
senses.why: Here the force is literal and the boundary is the body itself; the word's core of pressing through a limit reaches its most concrete and most serious point.
senses.whyCN: 此处强力是字面意义上的，界线就是身体本身；这个词「压过界限」的核心义在此到达最具体也最严重的程度。

senses.title: A foul in sport
senses.definition: an illegal move in a game that breaks its written rules and is punished by an official
senses.definitionCN: 比赛中破坏成文规则、由裁判加以处罚的违规动作
senses.example: The referee whistled a violation before the shot was taken.
senses.exampleCN: 投篮之前裁判就吹了一次犯规。
senses.why: A court is a rectangle of painted lines, so the original picture returns almost literally: a body moves across a line that the game forbids it to cross.
senses.whyCN: 球场就是由画线围出的矩形，最初的画面几乎原样复现：一具身体越过了比赛禁止它越过的线。

senses.title: An unlawful entry into territory
senses.titleCN: 对领地或领空的非法进入
senses.definition: the entering of airspace, waters or land without permission, treated as a breach of sovereignty
senses.definitionCN: 未经许可进入领空、领水或陆地，被视为对主权的破坏
senses.example: The drone's flight over the base was a violation of national airspace.
senses.exampleCN: 无人机飞越基地上空侵犯了国家领空。
senses.why: When the line is a border on a map, pressing through it becomes trespass; the same noun covers the aircraft that crosses without leave.
senses.whyCN: 当那条线是地图上的国界，强行穿过去就成了侵入；同一个名词也覆盖未经许可越界的飞行器。

intro.en: Violation is the noun of action from Latin violare 'to treat with force, violate'. The further origin of violare is disputed: it is often linked with vis 'force', but that link is not settled, so it is reported here as uncertain. English took the word through French and directly from Latin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: violation 是拉丁动词 violare「以强力对待、破坏」的动作名词。violare 更早的来源有争议：常被认为与 vis「力量」相关，但这一联系并未定论，故此处如实标注为存疑。英语经法语并直接从拉丁语吸收该词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Vis meant 'force, strength, violence'. Some accounts derive violare from it, but the derivation is contested and no single hypothesis is adopted here.
items.cn: vis 意为「力量、强度、暴力」。有说法认为 violare 由它派生，但此说存在争议，此处不选定论。

items.en: Violare is attested as 'to treat with force, to violate, to dishonour', used of laws, of women and of temples alike.
items.cn: violare 见于文献，意为「以强力对待、破坏、使蒙羞」，法律、人身与神庙都可作其对象。

items.en: Violatio, the noun of action, named the deed itself rather than the doer, and passed into the Romance languages.
items.cn: 动作名词 violatio 指行为本身而非行为人，并传入罗曼诸语。

items.en: The agent noun violator named the person who applies the force, an early sign that the family could name both deed and doer.
items.cn: 施事名词 violator 指施加强力的人，说明这一词族很早就能同时命名行为与行为人。

items.en: Old French carried the noun as violation in legal and religious texts, and its form, not the bare Latin stem, shaped the English spelling.
items.cn: 古法语在法律与宗教文本中沿用 violation 这一名词，英语的拼写形态来自它，而非裸露的拉丁词干。

items.en: English adopted violation for the breaking of a law, a oath or a sacred thing, and later extended it to rights, borders and games.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪吸收 violation，指对法律、誓言或神圣之物的破坏，后来又扩展到权利、边界与比赛。

note.en: The first group pairs two true relatives with two words that merely resemble the spelling; the second group offers near alternatives for the act of breaking a limit.
note.cn: 第一组把两个真正的同族词与两个只是拼写相似的词并列；第二组是「破坏界限」这一行为的近义替代。

entries.definition: To break a law, a right or something sacred; it is the verb that stands behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 破坏法律、权利或神圣之物；它是该名词背后的动词。

entries.definition: The person who breaks the law or the boundary; it names the agent where violation names the act.
entries.definitionCN: 破坏法律或界线的人；violation 指行为，它指行为人。

entries.definition: A small purple flower; it comes from Latin viola, the plant, and is only similar in spelling, not related in origin to violation.
entries.definitionCN: 一种紫色小花；出自拉丁语 viola（该植物），只是形近，与 violation 并非同源。

entries.definition: A stringed instrument; it comes through Italian from a medieval instrument name, and is only similar in sound, not related in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 一种弦乐器；经意大利语来自中古乐器名，只是读音形似，并非同源。

entries.definition: A breaking of a contract, duty or defence; it stresses the gap left behind, while violation stresses the force used.
entries.definitionCN: 对合同、义务或防线的破坏；它强调留下的缺口，而 violation 强调所用的强力。

entries.definition: An encroachment on a right, copyright or territory; it is the usual term in intellectual property, narrower than violation.
entries.definitionCN: 对权利、版权或领地的侵占；是知识产权领域的常用词，范围比 violation 窄。

entries.definition: A minor breach of a rule or law; it usually implies a small, punishable slip rather than a grave offence.
entries.definitionCN: 对规则或法律的轻微破坏；通常指可受处罚的小过失，而非严重罪行。

entries.definition: The act of treating a sacred place or object with contempt; it covers only the sacred branch of violation.
entries.definitionCN: 以轻蔑态度对待圣地或圣物的行为；只覆盖 violation 的神圣义分支。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb, the real action suffix and the real legal phrases that carry the word.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词、真实的动作名词后缀，以及承载该词的真实法律用语。

normal.en: Violare is 'to treat with force', so a violation is force applied where a limit should hold.
normal.cn: violare 意为「以强力对待」，所以 violation 就是在该有限制之处施加了强力。

normal.en: The suffix -tion turns the act of breaking into the thing broken: violate becomes violation.
normal.cn: 名词后缀把「破坏」的动作转为「所破坏之事」：violate 变成 violation。

normal.en: Legal phrases fix the object: traffic violation, violation of contract, violation of privacy.
normal.cn: 法律短语把对象固定下来：交通违规、违反合同、侵犯隐私。

normal.en: The agent is violator, the act is violation, the adjective is violative: three shapes of one stem.
normal.cn: 行为人是 violator，行为是 violation，形容词是 violative：同一词干的三种形态。

normal.en: A violation needs a line already drawn: no rule, no violation.
normal.cn: violation 需要一条早已画好的线：没有规则，就没有违反。

abstract.en: Picture a red line painted across a doorway and a heel landing beyond it in one stride.
abstract.cn: 想象门槛上刷着一道红线，一步之间鞋跟就落到了线外。

abstract.en: Picture a seal on a letter torn open from the wrong side, the wax split in two.
abstract.cn: 想象信封上的火漆印被人从内侧撕开，蜡一分为二。

abstract.en: Picture a rope around a temple door that someone has simply walked through, the rope still swinging.
abstract.cn: 想象神庙门前的绳子被人径直穿过，绳子还在晃。

examples.en: The factory was fined for repeated violations of the clean-air standards.
examples.cn: 这家工厂因多次违反清洁空气标准而被罚款。

examples.en: Sending her medical records to a third party was a clear violation of privacy.
examples.cn: 把她的病历发给第三方，明显侵犯了隐私。

examples.en: The umpire called a foot violation and awarded the point to the other side.
examples.cn: 裁判吹了脚部犯规，把这一分判给了对方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歪了，雷神」——把规矩歪着来，雷神都要劈下来：越线的举动 → 违反、违规

root: 拉丁 vis「力量」（与 violare 的联系存疑）→ violare「以强力对待、破坏」→ 动作名词 violatio → 古法语 violation → 英语 violation；名词后缀把「破坏」这一动作转为「所破坏之事」，同族有 violate、violator、inviolable。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one gesture: force applied across a limit. The limit may be a statute, a regulation, a contract, a right, a sacred place, a body, a touchline or a border; violation names the forcing through, and the register shifts with the object.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一个动作：把强力压过一道界限。这界限可以是成文法、条例、合同、权利、圣地、身体、边线或国界；violation 指强行穿过，语体则随对象而变化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot crossing a painted red line, a forbidden sign standing on the other side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚越过刷好的红线，另一侧立着禁止牌。

branches.en: LAW: the strongest line belongs to the state, and forcing past it produces the plain legal sense.
branches.cn: 法律：最强的线属于国家，强行越过它便产生最朴素的法律义。

branches.en: ADMINISTRATION: smaller authorities draw thinner lines, from parking rules to building codes.
branches.cn: 行政规管：较小的权威画出更细的线，从停车规定到建筑规范。

branches.en: CONTRACT: two parties draw the line together, so the breach injures a partner rather than the public.
branches.cn: 合同：线由双方共同画出，因此违反伤及的是合作方而非公众。

branches.en: THE PERSON AS BOUNDARY: privacy and the body are the innermost lines, and the force here becomes invasion.
branches.cn: 以人为界：隐私与身体是最内层的线，此处的强力便成了侵入。

branches.en: SACRED, PLAYFUL AND NATIONAL LINES: temples, touchlines and borders all repeat the same crossing under different guardians.
branches.cn: 神圣、竞技与国界之线：神庙、边线与国界，都在不同的守护者之下重复同一次越线。

intro.en: Violation is a Latin verb stem plus a Latin action suffix, and its family includes both agent nouns and negated adjectives.
intro.cn: violation 由一个拉丁动词词干加一个拉丁动作名词后缀构成，其词族既有施事名词，也有加否定成分的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin violare gave violatio and violator; adding the negative prefix in- yields the two adjectives inviolable and inviolate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 violare 衍生出 violatio 与 violator；加否定前缀则得到 inviolable 与 inviolate 两个形容词。

items.meaning: force; the act of breaking through
items.example: The stem carries the idea of force from the start.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干从一开始就带着「强力」的意思。

items.structure: violare (Latin verb, to treat with force)
items.example: The Latin verb covered laws, persons and temples.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词的对象包括法律、人与神庙。

items.meaning: to break a law or a boundary
items.example: Drivers who violate the speed limit are fined.

items.meaning: the act or instance of breaking a limit
items.meaningCN: 破坏界限的行为或事例
items.example: The violation was recorded on camera.
items.exampleCN: 这次违规被摄像头记录了下来。

items.example: Three violations were listed on the notice.
items.exampleCN: 通知上列出了三起违规。

items.example: The suffix turns a verb of action into a name for the deed.
items.exampleCN: 该后缀把动作动词变成对行为的称呼。

items.meaning: a person who breaks the limit
items.example: The violator refused to pay the fine.
The clause was held violative of the treaty.
items.exampleCN: 该条款被裁定违反了条约。

items.meaning: able to be broken or profaned
items.example: Even a strong oath is violable.
items.exampleCN: 再强的誓言也可能被违背。
该边界被宣布为不可侵犯。

items.example: The shrine remained inviolate for centuries.
items.exampleCN: 那座神殿数百年间未遭亵渎。

latinEntries.meaning: to treat with force; to violate; to dishonour
latinEntries.meaningCN: 以强力对待；破坏；使蒙羞
已被破坏的；遭强力对待的

definition_zh: 居住；存在于
definition_en: to live in a particular place, or to exist in something
core_image: 一栋房子门口钉着姓名牌，人长期住在里面
scene: 他在这条街住了二十年，却很少和邻居来往。 He has resided on this street for twenty years but rarely speaks to his neighbours.
sceneCN: 这里 reside 是「居住」（第 1 个义项：长期住在某处）；句意：他在这条街住了二十年，却很少和邻居来往。

senses.title: To live in a place
senses.definition: to live in a particular place for a long time
senses.definitionCN: 长期住在某个地方
senses.example: He has resided on this street for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他在这条街住了二十年。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to remain behind, which becomes settling and living somewhere.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「留在后面」，由此变成定居与居住。

senses.title: To exist in something
senses.definition: to be present as a quality or power in something
senses.definitionCN: 作为性质或力量存在于某物之中
senses.example: The value of the plan resides in its simplicity.
senses.exampleCN: 这项计划的价值在于它的简洁。
senses.why: A quality can be pictured as living inside the thing that shows it.
senses.whyCN: 一种性质可以被想象成住在展现它的那个事物里面。

senses.title: To be vested in someone
senses.definition: to belong to a person or body as a right or power
senses.definitionCN: 作为权利或权力归属于某人或机构
senses.example: Supreme power resides with the people.
senses.exampleCN: 最高权力属于人民。
senses.why: Power is thought of as dwelling in the body that holds it.
senses.whyCN: 权力被看作居住在掌握它的机构之中。

intro.en: Reside comes from Latin residere, to remain behind or settle, from re- and sedere, to sit.
intro.cn: reside 来自拉丁语 residere（留下、定居），由 re- 与 sedere（坐）构成。

items.en: Sedere means to sit.
items.cn: sedere 意为坐。

items.en: Residere means to remain behind or settle.
items.cn: residere 意为留在后面、定居。

items.en: Resider means to stay or dwell.
items.cn: resider 意为停留、居住。

items.en: Middle English residen means to dwell in a place.
items.cn: 中古英语 residen 意为在某地居住。

items.en: Reside is used for a person's fixed home.
items.cn: 到 15 世纪，reside 用于指人的固定住所。

items.en: Modern English adds the sense of a quality residing in something.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「性质存在于某物中」的义项。

note.en: Reside is a settling verb, and it sits near its noun family and near verbs for living and staying.
note.cn: reside 是一个「定居」动词，与名词词族以及表示居住和停留的动词相邻。

entries.definition: a home or the fact of living somewhere
entries.definitionCN: 住宅；居住

entries.definition: a person who lives in a place
entries.definitionCN: 居民

entries.definition: made up of homes
entries.definitionCN: 住宅的

entries.definition: to have your home in a place
entries.definitionCN: 居住

entries.definition: to live in a place, often literary
entries.definitionCN: 居住（较书面）

entries.definition: to remain in a place for a time
entries.definitionCN: 停留；暂住

normalIntro.en: Reside contains Latin sedere, to sit: to reside is to settle and stay.
normalIntro.cn: reside 含有拉丁语 sedere（坐）：居住就是安顿下来、留下来。

normal.en: Re- suggests staying in place, and sedere means sit.
normal.cn: re- 暗示留在原处，sedere 表示坐。

normal.en: Reside in a place is a formal way to say live there.
normal.cn: reside in a place 是「住在那里」的正式说法。

normal.en: The power to decide resides with the committee.
normal.cn: 决定权属于委员会。

normal.en: Residence and resident both grow from this verb.
normal.cn: residence 与 resident 都从这个动词生长出来。

normal.en: Compare live: live is everyday, while reside is formal.
normal.cn: 对比 live：live 是日常用语，reside 更正式。

abstract.en: Picture a nameplate fixed beside a door for years.
abstract.cn: 想象门边挂着一块多年的姓名牌。

abstract.en: Imagine roots spreading under a house.
abstract.cn: 想象树根在一座房子下面延伸。

abstract.en: Think of a thought living quietly inside a plan.
abstract.cn: 想象一个想法安静地住在一项计划里。

examples.en: He has resided on this street for twenty years.
examples.cn: 他在这条街住了二十年。

examples.en: The value of the plan resides in its simplicity.
examples.cn: 这项计划的价值在于它的简洁。

examples.en: Supreme power resides with the people.
examples.cn: 最高权力属于人民。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re + side」——一直待在这一边住下，就是居住；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sedere（坐）→ residere（留下、定居）→ 古法语 resider → 中古英语 residen → 现代英语 reside。

sensesIntro.en: The verb begins with the image of sitting down and staying, then extends to qualities that live inside things and powers that belong to a body.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从「坐下并留下」的画面开始，再扩展到「住在事物内部」的性质，以及「归属于某机构」的权力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person settled in one house and staying there.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人在一栋房子里安顿下来并长住。

branches.en: Living in a place is the core physical sense.
branches.cn: 在某地居住，是核心物理义项。

branches.en: A quality lives inside what shows it.
branches.cn: 性质住在展现它的东西里面。

branches.en: Power belongs to the body that holds it.
branches.cn: 权力归属于掌握它的机构。

branches.en: A person resides in a house, and a value resides in a plan.
branches.cn: 人住在房子里，价值住在计划里。

branches.en: Both qualities and powers are pictured as dwelling somewhere.
branches.cn: 性质与权力都被想象成「住在某处」。

intro.en: Reside is a Latin verb carried through French, with English endings forming its noun and adjective family.
intro.cn: reside 是经法语传递的拉丁动词，名词与形容词词族由英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin sedere means to sit, and residere means to remain behind or settle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sedere 意为坐，residere 意为留下、定居。

items.example: Re- adds the sense of remaining.
Residere joins the prefix and the root.
items.exampleCN: residere 把前缀与词根结合。

items.example: Resider carries the verb into French.
items.exampleCN: resider 把这个动词带入法语。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或动作的词尾

definition_zh: n. 极度的痛苦；煎熬 v. 使极度痛苦；感到煎熬
definition_en: Severe mental or physical suffering, especially from loss or worry; as a verb, to cause or feel such suffering.
core_image: 心里被拧成一股绳，久久松不开
scene: 她在医院走廊里等了整夜，一句话也说不出。 His face showed the anguish of that long wait.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：整夜等待带来的不是普通难过，而是被拧住般的极度煎熬，这就是 anguish。

forms.label: 过去式与过去分词（动词）

senses.title: Severe suffering of mind or body
senses.definition: extreme distress caused by loss, fear or pain, beyond ordinary sadness
senses.definitionCN: 由丧失、恐惧或疼痛引起的极度苦恼，超出一般的难过
senses.example: The family waited in anguish for news of the boat.
senses.exampleCN: 那家人在煎熬中等待船的消息。
senses.why: The root means to choke or squeeze, so anguish is distress pictured as a narrowing: the chest tightens and nothing can pass.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「使窒息、挤压」，所以 anguish 是把苦恼想象成「变窄」：胸口收紧，什么都过不去。

senses.title: To suffer or to cause suffering
senses.definition: to feel or inflict severe distress, a literary verbal use
senses.definitionCN: 感到或施加极度苦恼，是较书面的动词用法
senses.example: She anguished over the letter for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 她为那封信煎熬了整整一周。
senses.why: The verb keeps the same squeeze, but now it is something a person does over time rather than a state they are in.
senses.whyCN: 动词保留同一种「拧紧」，只是它变成了一个人持续做的动作，而不是所处的状态。

intro.en: Anguish comes from Latin angustia, distress or narrowness, from angere, to choke. Old French anguisse kept the choking image, and Middle English took it as anguisshe.
intro.cn: anguish 来自拉丁语 angustia「苦恼、狭窄」，出自 angere「使窒息」。古法语 anguisse 保留了「窒息」意象，中古英语借为 anguisshe。

items.en: Latin angere meant to choke, squeeze or strangle. The same root gives angina, anxious, anger and the Latin angustus, narrow.
items.cn: 拉丁语 angere 意为「使窒息、挤压、勒紧」。同一词根产生 angina、anxious、anger 以及拉丁语 angustus「狭窄的」。

items.en: Angustia named tightness and, figuratively, distress: the feeling of being in a narrow place with no room to move.
items.cn: angustia 指「紧窄」，引申为「苦恼」：身处狭窄之地、无处可动的感觉。

items.en: Old French anguisse and angoisse kept the physical sense of a choking sensation in the throat, which is still visible in modern French angoisse.
items.cn: 古法语 anguisse 与 angoisse 保留了「喉部窒息感」的身体义，现代法语 angoisse 中仍可见到。

items.en: Middle English took the word as anguisshe in the thirteenth century, used for both bodily pain and spiritual torment.
items.cn: 中古英语在 13 世纪借为 anguisshe，既指肉体疼痛，也指精神折磨。

items.en: Modern anguish is mostly mental and literary, and the verb use, to anguish over something, is newer and less common.
items.cn: 现代 anguish 多指精神层面且偏书面，动词用法「为某事煎熬」较新且不常见。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against languish, which means to weaken slowly; the near-meaning group lists other words for extreme suffering.
note.cn: 形近组提醒别与 languish「渐渐衰弱」混淆；近义组列出其他表示极度痛苦的词。

entries.definition: Showing severe distress.
entries.definitionCN: 显出极度苦恼的。

entries.definition: To grow weak or be left to suffer.
entries.definitionCN: 渐渐衰弱或被弃置受苦。

entries.definition: Chest pain from a short of blood.
entries.definitionCN: 心肌缺血引起的胸痛。

entries.definition: Strong displeasure, often outward.
entries.definitionCN: 强烈的不快，常向外发作。

entries.definition: Extreme physical or mental pain.
entries.definitionCN: 极度的肉体或精神疼痛。

entries.definition: Severe and prolonged suffering.
entries.definitionCN: 严重而持久的折磨。

entries.definition: Great worry, pain or danger.
entries.definitionCN: 极大的忧虑、痛苦或危难。

entries.definition: Deep sorrow after a death.
entries.definitionCN: 亲人去世后的深切悲伤。

normalIntro.en: Anguish shares its squeeze root with anger and angina: picture a throat tightening.
normalIntro.cn: anguish 与 anger、angina 共用「挤压」词根：想象喉咙在收紧。

normal.en: The noun is usually uncountable: in anguish, not in an anguish.
normal.cn: 名词通常不可数：in anguish，不说 in an anguish。

normal.en: The verb pattern is anguish over something.
normal.cn: 动词格式是 anguish over something。

normal.en: Anguished is the common adjective: an anguished cry.
normal.cn: anguished 是常用形容词：一声痛苦的喊叫。

normal.en: Do not confuse anguish with languish, to weaken slowly.
normal.cn: 别把 anguish 与 languish「渐渐衰弱」混淆。

normal.en: Anguish is stronger than distress and more inward than anger.
normal.cn: anguish 比 distress 更重，比 anger 更向内。

abstract.en: Picture a corridor where someone waits all night.
abstract.cn: 想象一条有人等了整夜的走廊。

abstract.en: Imagine a rope twisted tighter with every hour.
abstract.cn: 想象一根每小时都被拧得更紧的绳。

abstract.en: Think of a letter that cannot be sent or torn up.
abstract.cn: 想象一封既寄不出也撕不掉的信。

examples.en: The decision caused her months of anguish.
examples.cn: 这个决定让她煎熬了好几个月。

examples.en: He anguished over whether to tell the truth.
examples.cn: 他为是否说出真相而煎熬。

examples.en: Her anguished face said more than words could.
examples.cn: 她痛苦的表情胜过千言万语。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「安哥卫士」——安（an）哥（gu）卫士（ish）：卫士守着一夜不眠，心里被拧住，就是极度煎熬 anguish。

root: 拉丁语 angere「使窒息」生出 angustia「紧窄、苦恼」，经古法语 anguisse 入中古英语 anguisshe，今作 anguish，字面即「被拧到无处可动的痛苦」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one tightening: the state of being squeezed by loss or fear, and the act of twisting over a choice.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一次拧紧：被丧失或恐惧攥住的状态，以及为一个选择反复拧心的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the mind twisted into a rope that will not slacken
core.cn: 核心意象：心被拧成一股松不开的绳

branches.en: A night spent waiting for news.
branches.cn: 等消息等了一整夜。

branches.en: A grief too heavy to speak.
branches.cn: 重到说不出口的悲伤。

branches.en: A week of twisting over one letter.
branches.cn: 为一封信拧心了一周。

branches.en: A choice that keeps returning at night.
branches.cn: 一个夜里不断回来的选择。

branches.en: The same squeeze, as state then as act.
branches.cn: 同一次拧紧，先是状态，再是动作。

intro.en: Anguish keeps the squeeze root ang- and the -ish ending, and the same root builds anger, angina and anxious.
intro.cn: anguish 保留「挤压」词根 ang- 与 -ish 词尾，同一词根还构成 anger、angina 与 anxious。

latinIntro.en: Latin angere, to choke, gives angustia, narrowness; Old French anguisse passed it on, and the same root is behind angina.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 angere「使窒息」产生 angustia「狭窄」；古法语 anguisse 把它传下来，同一词根也是 angina 的来源。

items.exampleCN: 令人煎熬的；令人不安的

latinEntries.example: Angere is the root of the family.
Angoisse still means anxiety in French.
latinEntries.exampleCN: angoisse 在法语中仍指焦虑。

definition_zh: 基因型；一个生物体的遗传组成
definition_en: the genetic constitution of an organism, especially the combination of alleles at one or more loci
core_image: 同一株植物在不同土壤里外形不同，但根里那套指令始终一致
scene: 同一株植物在不同土壤里长得不一样，但根里的指令相同。 Two plants may share a genotype yet look completely different.
sceneCN: 这里 genotype 指「生物体内部的遗传组成」（第 1 个义项：全部遗传指令的组合）；句意为两株植物可以基因型相同，外表却完全不同。可辨识物件：两盆植物、不同土壤、根系示意图、指令卡片。

senses.title: The inherited constitution
senses.definition: the complete set of inherited instructions in an organism
senses.definitionCN: 一个生物体所继承的全部指令集合
senses.example: The genotype of an organism is its full set of inherited instructions.
senses.exampleCN: 一个生物体的基因型就是它所继承的全部指令。
senses.why: Johannsen coined the word to separate what is inherited from what is seen, so genotype names the internal constitution.
senses.whyCN: 约翰森造这个词是为了把「遗传的」与「看见的」分开，因此基因型命名内部组成。

senses.title: Genotype contrasted with phenotype
senses.titleCN: 与表现型相对的基因型
senses.definition: the inherited constitution considered apart from its observable expression
senses.definitionCN: 与其可观察表现分开考虑的遗传组成
senses.example: Two mice with the same genotype can differ in phenotype.
senses.exampleCN: 基因型相同的两只小鼠可以有不同的表现型。
senses.why: The pair genotype and phenotype was coined together, and each word is defined by its contrast with the other.
senses.whyCN: 基因型与表现型是成对造出的，每个词都通过与另一个词对照而获得定义。

senses.title: Genotype at one locus
senses.definition: the combination of alleles at a specified genetic locus
senses.definitionCN: 在特定位点上等位基因的组合
senses.example: The genotype at that locus was heterozygous in half the sample.
senses.exampleCN: 该位点的基因型在样本中有一半是杂合的。
senses.why: The word narrowed from the whole constitution to the allele pair at one address, especially in laboratory genetics.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从整体组成收窄到某一地址上的等位基因对，尤其在实验室遗传学中。

senses.title: Genotype testing
senses.definition: laboratory testing that identifies a specific inherited constitution
senses.definitionCN: 识别特定遗传组成的实验室检测
senses.example: Genotype testing identifies carriers before symptoms appear.
senses.exampleCN: 基因型检测在症状出现前识别携带者。
senses.why: Testing turns the abstract constitution into a result that can guide decisions.
senses.whyCN: 检测把抽象的组成变成可指导决策的结果。

senses.title: Genotype frequency
senses.definition: the proportion of individuals in a group with a given genotype
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体中具有某一基因型的个体比例
senses.example: Genotype frequencies shift under selection.
senses.exampleCN: 基因型频率在选择作用下发生移动。
senses.why: Population genetics counts constitutions, so the word becomes a frequency rather than a property of one body.
senses.whyCN: 群体遗传学对组成进行计数，因此这个词成为频率，而非单个身体的性质。

senses.title: The genotype-phenotype map
senses.titleCN: 基因型与表现型的对应关系
senses.definition: the relationship by which inherited constitution produces observable traits
senses.definitionCN: 遗传组成产生可观察性状的对应关系
senses.example: The genotype-phenotype map is rarely one to one.
senses.exampleCN: 基因型与表现型的对应关系很少是一对一的。
senses.why: The compound marks the central problem of genetics: many instructions can lead to one form, and one instruction to many forms.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词标记遗传学的核心难题：多套指令可以导致一种形态，一套指令也可以导致多种形态。

senses.title: Classification by genotype
senses.definition: grouping organisms by inherited constitution rather than by appearance
senses.definitionCN: 按遗传组成而非外表对生物分组
senses.example: Breeders group animals by genotype rather than appearance.
senses.exampleCN: 育种者按基因型而非外表给动物分组。
senses.why: When appearance misleads, classification moves to the constitution, which is why genotype becomes a sorting label.
senses.whyCN: 当外表会误导时，分类转向内部组成，因此基因型成为分类标签。

senses.title: Genotype in microbiology
senses.definition: the inherited constitution of a virus or microbe, often used to trace strains
senses.definitionCN: 病毒或微生物的遗传组成，常用于追踪毒株
senses.example: The viral genotype determines which cells it can enter.
senses.exampleCN: 病毒的基因型决定它能进入哪些细胞。
senses.why: In microbiology the word often names a strain marker, since small genomes make the constitution easy to compare.
senses.whyCN: 在微生物学中，这个词常命名毒株标记，因为小基因组使组成易于比较。

intro.en: Genotype was introduced by Wilhelm Johannsen in 1909 as German Genotypus, joining genos 'race, kind' with typos 'impression, mold'.
intro.cn: genotype 由威廉·约翰森于 1909 年以德语 Genotypus 引入，把 genos「种族、种类」与 typos「印痕、模子」结合起来。

items.en: Genos 'race, kind' belongs to the PIE family reconstructed as *ǵenh₁-; the root form is a reconstruction, and Latin genus is a cognate rather than the source.
items.cn: genos「种族、种类」属于被重构为 *ǵenh₁- 的原始印欧语词族；该词根形式是重构，拉丁 genus 是同源词而非来源。

items.en: Typos meant 'impression, mold, model'; it also appears in phenotype, typography and in Latin typus, a loan from Greek.
items.cn: typos 意为「印痕、模子、模型」；它也出现在 phenotype、typography 以及借自希腊的拉丁 typus 中。

items.en: Johannsen used German Genotypus in 1909 to name the inherited constitution, in deliberate contrast with the visible result.
items.cn: 约翰森在 1909 年使用德语 Genotypus，命名遗传组成，刻意与可见结果相对。

items.en: English genotype is recorded by 1910; spelling and first date vary between Genotypus and genotype, and early translations complicate the record.
items.cn: 英语 genotype 在 1910 年前已有记录；Genotypus 与 genotype 的拼写和首见年代各有差异，早期翻译使记录更复杂。

items.en: The word moved from the whole constitution to the allele combination at a single locus, a narrower laboratory use.
items.cn: 这个词从整体组成转向单位点的等位基因组合，这是更窄的实验室用法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first English date and spelling): the coinage is documented, but the route into English is not precisely dated, and no Latin derivative of the compound exists, so latinEntries is empty.
items.cn: 来源不确定（英语首见年代与拼写）：造词有文献可查，但进入英语的路径没有精确年代；该复合词没有拉丁派生词，因此 latinEntries 留空。

note.en: Group one separates genotype from its paired and same-root terms plus one accidental look-alike; group two separates it from the observable and the carrier concepts.
note.cn: 第一组把 genotype 与成对词、同根词及一个偶然形近词分开；第二组把它与「可观察」和「载体」概念区分。

entries.definition: The observable traits produced by the genotype plus environment; the two words were coined as a pair.
entries.definitionCN: 由基因型与环境共同产生的可观察性状；两词是成对造出的。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'of a genotype'; it does not name the constitution itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「基因型的」的形容词；它不命名组成本身。

entries.definition: The entire genetic material; the genotype is the constitution with respect to particular loci or alleles.
entries.definitionCN: 指全部遗传物质；基因型是就特定位点或等位基因而言的组成。

entries.definition: From Greek karyon 'nut, kernel' plus typos: the number and appearance of chromosomes, not the allele constitution.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 karyon「核、仁」加 typos：指染色体的数目与外观，而非等位基因组成。

entries.definition: What can be seen or measured; genotype is the inherited instruction behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 可见或可测的结果；基因型是它背后的遗传指令。

entries.definition: The complete sequence; genotype is a description of constitution at specified loci.
entries.definitionCN: 指完整序列；基因型是对特定位点组成的描述。

entries.definition: One alternative form at a locus; a genotype is the combination of such forms.
entries.definitionCN: 指某位点的一种备选形式；基因型是这类形式的组合。

entries.definition: A lineage of organisms with a shared background; genotype is the precise constitution used to define it.
entries.definitionCN: 指共享背景的生物谱系；基因型是用来界定它的精确组成。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: genos 'kind' + typos 'mold': the kind stamped inside.
normal.cn: genos「种类」+ typos「模子」：印在内部的那个种类。

normal.en: The pair is genotype and phenotype: inside versus outside.
normal.cn: 成对词是 genotype 与 phenotype：内部对表面。

normal.en: The family runs genotype, genotypic, genotypically and phenotype.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 genotype、genotypic、genotypically 与 phenotype。

normal.en: At one locus, genotype means the allele pair.
normal.cn: 在单个位点上，基因型指等位基因对。

normal.en: Genotype testing looks at the constitution before symptoms.
normal.cn: 基因型检测在症状出现前查看组成。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed blueprint that may be built in several different ways.
abstract.cn: 想象一张密封蓝图，可以用几种不同方式建造。

abstract.en: Picture the same recipe cooked in two kitchens with different results.
abstract.cn: 想象同一份食谱在两个厨房做出不同结果。

abstract.en: Picture a locked box whose label describes the contents, not the contents themselves.
abstract.cn: 想象一只锁着的箱子，标签描述内容，却不等于内容。

examples.en: The genotype of each seedling was recorded before planting.
examples.cn: 每株幼苗的基因型在栽种前被记录。

examples.en: Genotype frequencies changed after the drought.
examples.cn: 干旱之后基因型频率发生变化。

examples.en: The viral genotype was used to trace the outbreak.
examples.cn: 病毒基因型被用来追踪疫情。

dict_mnemonic.text: geno（种类）+ type（模子）——内部印着的那套模子 → 基因型；与 phenotype（表现型）成对。

root: 希腊 genos「种族、种类」+ typos「印痕、模子」；约翰森 1909 年以德语 Genotypus 造词；genos 出自原始印欧语 *ǵenh₁-（重构形式）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow an inner constitution: the whole set, its contrast with phenotype, one locus, a test, a frequency, a map, a classification and a strain marker.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一份内部组成展开：整套、与表现型的对照、单个位点、检测、频率、对应图、分类与毒株标记。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one plant, two soils, two shapes, one identical set of instructions in the roots.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一株植物，两种土壤，两种外形，根里却是同一套指令。

branches.en: THE CONSTITUTION: the full inherited instruction set of one organism.
branches.cn: 组成：一个生物体所继承的完整指令集。

branches.en: THE PAIR AND THE MAP: what is inherited versus what is seen, and how the two connect.
branches.cn: 成对与对应：遗传之物对可见之物，以及两者如何连接。

branches.en: LOCUS AND CLASSIFICATION: the allele pair at one address, and sorting by constitution.
branches.cn: 位点与分类：某一地址上的等位基因对，以及按组成归类。

branches.en: TEST AND FREQUENCY: a result that guides decisions, and a proportion in a group.
branches.cn: 检测与频率：指导决策的结果，以及群体中的比例。

branches.en: STRAIN MARKER: in microbes, the constitution used to trace a lineage.
branches.cn: 毒株标记：在微生物中，用来追踪谱系的组成。

intro.en: Genotype joins two Greek elements; the second, typos, also builds phenotype and a family of type words.
intro.cn: genotype 结合两个希腊成分；第二个成分 typos 还构成 phenotype 及一批以 type 结尾的词。

latinIntro.en: Greek genos gives the first element, typos the second. The same typos appears in phenotype, karyotype and typography. No Latin derivative of the compound exists, so latinEntries is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 genos 提供第一个成分，typos 提供第二个。同一 typos 还出现在 phenotype、karyotype 与 typography 中。该复合词没有拉丁派生词，因此 latinEntries 留空。

items.example: The first element names the kind.
The second element names the stamp or pattern.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分命名印记或模式。

items.example: The combining form joins genotype and genome.
items.exampleCN: 这个组合形式连接 genotype 与 genome。

items.example: The suffix also appears in phenotype and karyotype.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀也出现在 phenotype 与 karyotype 中。
这些品系在基因型上不同。

items.example: The karyotype showed an extra chromosome.
items.exampleCN: 核型显示多了一条染色体。
